Meta-analytic studies on self-directed parenting interventions have shown moderate to large effects on children's behavior problems compared to waitlist control groups (Baumel et al., 2016; Tarver et al., 2014). The studies in these meta-analyses included interventions with or without therapist support (e.g. video-tape training, online parent training, and workbook training) for (mostly recruited) children with disruptive behavior problems. Only one of the studies that were included in these meta-analyses was conducted specifically in children with ADHD (Daley and O'Brien, 2013). This study showed that self-directed parent training was effective on the reduction of ADHD symptoms in 4 to 11 year old referred children, compared to a waitlist control group. Parents in this study attended a face-to-face introduction, after which they received a written manual in which they worked for six weeks while receiving weekly phone calls (i.e. to remind and monitor, non-therapeutic). Another study (not included in the meta-analyses of Baumel et al. (2016) and Tarver et al. (2014)) demonstrated that online parent training was effective in reducing behavioral problems in recruited preschool children with ADHD symptoms (Franke et al., 2016). After receiving online parent training, consisting of eight online modules and two telephone consultations, mothers in this study reported improved child behavior in contrast with a delayed intervention group. There are also few studies that have compared self-directed parent training to their therapist-led equivalents. In the above mentioned meta-analysis (Tarver et al., 2014) four of such studies, focusing on children with either oppositional or conduct problems, were included. No significant differences were found in the decrease of externalizing problems between the self-directed and therapist-led parent training formats. Another meta-analysis (Lundahl et al., 2006) examined treatment modality as a moderator for the effect of parent training programs targeting disruptive child behaviors. Across studies, no significant difference was found between the effect of self-directed and therapist-led interventions on child behavior. To our knowledge, only one study investigated the effect of self-directed and therapist-led parent training in relation to ADHD (DuPaul et al., 2018). This study used a randomized controlled pilot with recruited preschool children at risk for ADHD and demonstrated that both a therapist-led group parent training and an online parent training (consisting of a first face-to-face session, ten online sessions, and weekly telephone contact) resulted in improved child behavior in comparison to a waitlist control group. In general, self-directed parenting interventions differ in the amount of therapist support. Studies have shown that therapist support (e.g. telephone contact, online contact, face-to-face appointments), can positively affect the effects of these programs (Day and Sanders, 2018; O'Brien and Daley, 2011; Tarver et al., 2014; Webster-Stratton, 1990).

Solms-Laubach (water hyacinth) has been reported to be highly effective in removing HMs and other contaminants from polluted water bodies (Mishra and Tripathi, 2008; Mishra and Tripathi, 2009; Odjegba and Fasidi, 2004; Tchounwou et al., 2014). Water hyacinths are free-floating perennial herbs belonging to the family Pontederiaceae (Gopal, 1987). These plants are native to South America, but have now invaded many tropical and subtropical regions including Asia, Africa and Australia (Tellez et al., 2008). Their rapid growth rate, easy propagation through stolons and vegetative reproduction make these plants ideal candidates for phytoremediation purposes (Arora et al., 2004). However, despite the well-documented ability of water hyacinths to remove HMs from contaminated waters, there are few studies on the use of these plants in remediating Cu-contaminated soils (Alvarado et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2015b; Dias Leles et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2007; Muramoto and Oki, 1983; Varela et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2015). This study aims to assess the phytoremediation capability of E. crassipes for Cu-contaminated soils. Specifically, the objectives were: (1) to determine the effect of Cu concentration on the growth performance of E. crassipes; (2) to evaluate the phytoextraction efficiency of E. crassipes; and (3) to identify the distribution of Cu in the plant parts. The experimental design used in this study was completely randomized design (CRD) with five treatments replicated thrice. A total of fifteen pots were utilized for the experiment. Each pot contained approximately 10 kg of sandy loam soil collected from the upland area of the University of the Philippines Los Banos (UPLB) campus. Soil characterization prior to planting revealed a pH of 7.43, electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.27 dS/m, cation exchange capacity (CEC) of 24 cmol/kg, and total nitrogen content of 0.04%. The initial Cu level of the soil was below detectable limits ( 1/2g/g). The soil samples were air dried, crushed using wooden mallet and sieved through a 2 mm sieve. Prior to planting, each pot was fertilized with 100 g urea and 50 g triple superphosphate.

As John's fingers brushed against her skin, he felt a surge of panic course through his veins. He tried to shake her awake, but she remained still, her head lolling to one side. The silence was oppressive, punctuated only by the distant hum of the city and the soft creaking of the car's suspension. John's mind raced as he tried to process what was happening. They had been driving home from the real estate agent's office, celebrating their new home, and now...now Mary was lying unconscious in the passenger seat. He checked her pulse, his heart pounding in his chest. It was steady, thank God. He took a deep breath and tried to think clearly. They were on a side street, away from the main roads. He couldn't see any other cars or pedestrians nearby. He glanced around, taking in their surroundings. They were in a rundown part of town, with crumbling buildings and overgrown gardens. Not exactly the most welcoming neighborhood. John's eyes snapped back to Mary's face. He had to get her to a hospital. He tried to start the car, but it wouldn't budge. The impact had apparently damaged the engine. He was stranded, with his unconscious wife lying beside him. Panic set in as he scrambled out of the car, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. He looked around again, this time taking in the dark alleys and deserted streets. He was alone, with no phone signal and no way to get help. As the night wore on, John's thoughts grew darker. He was trapped, with no way to save Mary. The city seemed to be closing in around him, the shadows cast by the streetlights twisting into sinister shapes. He felt like he was drowning, suffocating under the weight of his own helplessness. And then, just as he thought things couldn't get any worse, he heard the sound of footsteps crunching through the gravel behind him.

Well, Springwood isn't much of a place to remember, truth be told. Just one of those tiny dots on a map where people only pass through without giving a second thought. But it's home, or at least, it was. Mary gave him a soft smile, "Home is where the heart is, as they say. But here, we try to make something close to it. A place where you can catch your breath before life decides to throw you into another storm." The corners of Jacob's mouth twitched. "Yeah, that's what I'm hoping for." "Take it easy on him, Mary. Let the boy breathe. We all know how suffocating this place can feel at first," David added with a chuckle, his voice rich like warm molasses. Mary waved him off, her attention still focused on Jacob. "We've got rules here, Jacob, but they're fair. We ask for respect, kindness, and that you try to abide by curfew-9 p.m. sharp. Other than that, you're free to be who you need to be." "That sounds fair," Jacob responded, nodding slightly, feeling both the comfort and the expectations that the couple's words wrapped around him like an old, woolen shawl. David leaned closer, his eyes glinting with curiosity. "So, what brings you from this Springwood of yours?" Jacob paused, taking a moment to gather his thoughts. There was so much unsaid, tangled in the shadows of his mind. He decided on a cautious truth. "I'm trying to find something... something more, I guess." "Isn't everyone?" Karen chimed in, wrapping an arm around Jacob's shoulder with a sisterly squeeze. "This place could grow on you if you let it." The warmth of their unexpected kindness felt like a wave he wasn't sure how to navigate, and so he changed the topic to safer shores. "What's the plan for this evening?" "Oh, just a little welcome supper for you," Mary answered, bustling around the kitchen, her movements graceful yet hurried like a seasoned dancer. David smirked, "And believe me, you haven't lived until you've tried Mary's roast beef. It could make a grown man weep." Karen gave a playful eye-roll. "He's exaggerating, but it's pretty good, I'll give her that." "Great, I could eat a horse," Jacob said, a hunger he hadn't allowed himself to feel for days grumbling to life in his stomach. As the evening unfolded, the house slowly came alive. Other kids darted in from various corners of the streets, laughing, teasing, bringing with them the scent of rain and the sharp edge of city life. They shared stories-mundane and extraordinary-over steaming plates of food, clattering forks, and glasses filled with whatever drink wisdom dictated. For the first time since leaving Springwood, Jacob felt the faint, pulsing warmth of something safe, something like belonging, creeping into his bones. It wasn't perfect, and it certainly wasn't permanent, but it was enough for tonight. As laughter filled the room, Jacob allowed himself a small sigh of relief, a moment's peace, just a breath before facing whatever dreams or nightmares lay beyond, waiting for him in the darkness of night and the shimmering web of his tomorrows.

In one of these studies, researchers found that infants who were classified as recognizers on the MSR exhibited better memory for the location of a hidden object 12 months later, a finding that is consistent with the hypothesized relationship between cognitive self-representation and memory organization (Howe et al., 1993) and consistent with the hypothesis that MSR indexes a cognitive self-awareness. Nevertheless, despite being the dominant measure of emerging self-awareness, there is still no general acceptance of the claim that the MSR test reflects a developing self-awareness (for critics see Heyes, 1994; Mitchell, 1993a,b), and some have argued that it may instead reflect an understanding of the properties of mirrors (Loveland, 1986), or differences in the extent to which toddlers are either able or motivated to touch the mark (Asendorpf et al., 1996). Studying the development of self-awareness in toddlers is challenging as they cannot report on how they process self-related stimuli. Therefore, our current knowledge of early self-awareness is limited, while much work in adult cognitive neuroscience has already made significant progress in identifying the neural underpinnings of self-related processing. Specifically, a network of brain regions which is activated during passive rest (i.e. resting-state) in the low-frequency range (<0.1 Hz), appears to be recruited during self-related processing (Raichle, 2015). This so-called Default Mode Network (DMN), which overlaps considerably with the social brain network (Mars et al., 2012), is composed of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), the precuneus, the posterior and anterior cingulate cortex, the inferior parietal lobe (IPL), the medial temporal lobe and the temporoparietal junction (TPJ) (Davey et al., 2016; Greicius et al., 2003; Harrison et al., 2008; Mars et al., 2012; Molnar-Szakacs and Uddin, 2013; Raichle, 2015; Schilbach et al., 2008; Sporns, 2010). The DMN is thought to play a pivotal role in several introspective and adaptive mental activities, such as autobiographical memory (Philippi et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2013), theory of mind and mentalizing (Li et al., 2014; Mars et al., 2012), and planning and envisioning future events (Ostby et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2016). Self-referential mental processing is the common feature of most of the processes which elicit DMN engagement, suggesting that this network is our 'intrinsic system' for dealing with self-related processing (Davey et al., 2016; Golland et al., 2008; Molnar-Szakacs and Uddin, 2013; Raichle, 2015; Sporns, 2010). Consistent with this idea, recent fMRI studies have shown the engagement of core areas of the DMN in self-processing tasks in adults (Davey et al., 2016; Kaplan et al., 2008; Kelley et al., 2002; Kircher et al., 2000; Uddin et al., 2005). The fact that the activity elicited by self-processing tasks is remarkably similar to the activation of the DMN during rest, led to the hypothesis that during quiet rest there is a shift from perceiving the external world to internal modes of cognition (Buckner and Carroll, 2007).

And if epilepsy played a role in the wreck, it only bolsters their belief he shouldn't have been driving in the first place. "Why could somebody let this happen?" Xue's mother, Sun Chun Zhi, asked through a translator. "Obviously, he had a history of driving recklessly and had violated many traffic laws." Chinese laws would've never let someone like Skaggs drive, and more frustratingly, they say, the Chinese government would've stepped in with financial help if this had happened in their homeland. Conversely, it is a Chinese law that has been most devastating. Because the world's most populous nation has for 30 years enforced a one-child-per-couple policy, Bian, Xue and Sun Yan had no siblings, so the families' prospects for the future were crushed in a Ford Taurus at the intersection of Urbana and Moorefield roads. "When you raise a child in China, you are basically insuring your old age," Sun Yan's mother, Yu Ming, said, weeping as she spoke through a translator. Because Bian, Xue and Sun Yan had promising futures, their parents were confident asking friends, relatives, colleagues and even their kids' classmates for money to send them to graduate school at the 1,500-student Urbana University. In China, personal loans from banks aren't as common as they are in the U.S. More commonly, people borrow from friends and family, and you are honor bound to pay them back. There is no poor-mouthing or filing for bankruptcy. The university unveiled a memorial last year among three Lacebark Pines, a native Chinese tree. "You return what you owe. It is the bible of heaven and the ground rule of Earth," Yu said, using a Chinese saying to explain the importance of honoring your debts. Each family borrowed in the neighborhood of 300,000 yuan, almost $44,000, to send their kids 6,500 miles to Urbana University. They each borrowed tens of thousands of dollars more for their children's funerals and several trips to the United States, some to attend Skaggs' trial. They've collectively received about $19,000 from a state victim's fund and $22,000 from a charitable fund established by Urbana University. Another fund set up by the university collected about $36,000, but much of the money went toward the families' funeral and travel bills. The mothers say they appreciate the donations because their pensions and pay are a pittance of what they owe. Xue's father is back home in Dalian City, a trading hub of about 6 million people on the Liaodong Peninsula near North Korea. The retired office manager earns a pension of about 1,600 yuan, or $234, a month. Bian's father and Sun Yan's father live in Shenyang, an industrial base of more than 7 million people, also near North Korea. Bian's father has been working all the overtime shifts he can muster and brings home about 3,500 yuan ($512) a month.

As fighting continued for the last bastions under Gadhafi's grip, the longtime dictator's whereabouts remained unknown to rebel authorities. A clue came from a 17-year-old who told Sky News he had seen Gadhafi on Friday at the compound in Tripoli belonging to one of Gadhafi's sons, Khamis. The teen said he had been working for the previous month as a guard for Khamis Gadhafi. The leader arrived and spoke with his son for 10 to 15 minutes, Abdu Salam Ataher-Ali said. Friday's visit by Moammar Gadhafi came as rebels were taking control of the capital and Gadhafi loyalists were preparing to flee, the teenager told a translator during an interview in a rebel compound. "He said Gadhafi was visiting us at the same time when we run away from Khamis' compound," the translator said. During the visit, the leader's daughter, Aisha, arrived at the compound, where she and her father got into a convoy of vehicles and drove off, the teen told the translator. "He said one of the high-ranking soldiers come to us and we asked him, 'Where is Gadhafi going?' and he said 'To Sabha,' " the teen said. Sabha is a city in southwestern Libya and one of the loyalist strongholds. Khamis Gadhafi then got into an armored Toyota Land Cruiser and drove toward the town of Bani Walid, the teen said. Bani Walid is a city in the Misrata District in the north, another Gadhafi stronghold. An armored Land Cruiser was among a number of vehicles that were destroyed later by NATO bombs along the road northward. But it was not clear whether Khamis died in that attack. Tripoli residents greeted the end of Ramadan with celebratory gunfire amid news of Khamis' death Sunday night after a battle with rebel forces in northwest Libya between Tarunah and Bani Walid. A rebel commander said Khamis Gadhafi was buried in the area. The teen said he had been persuaded to join Khamis Gadhafi's group when he was told that foreign forces were attacking the country, Sky News reported. CNN has not been able to verify the Sky News report. Khamis Gadhafi's legacy includes his eponymous Khamis Brigade, also known as the 32nd Brigade, which has been accused of human rights abuses. Human Rights Watch said Monday that the brigade executed detainees a week ago in a warehouse near Tripoli. Forces led by Khamis Gadhafi also killed scores of captive civilians as they tried to retreat from Tripoli, according to Muneer Masoud Own, who survived the attack, and CNN's Arwa Damon, who saw the bodies being hauled off. Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International both documented the alleged incident. The legacy also apparently includes Shywega Mullah, who told CNN she worked as a nanny for Hannibal Gadhafi, one of Moammar Gadhafi's sons.

But it's when you look past that, to move beyond the gimmick, that the show reveals its treasure. Larry Appleton's constant schemes are a source of unparalleled amusement. Everytime he tries to get rich, score on a date, or even just get a date, he cannot proceed but under the aegis of a bizarre and outlandish plan. These machinations, usually invented to cover a previous transgression, inevitably explode into problems far larger than those they had originally been drafted to obfuscate. Watching him get into trouble, and especially watching him try to weasel out of it, are my most cherished memories of the TGiF line up. Sports Night: If you haven't seen this show, stop reading and rent (or buy) the DVD's. Sports Night is a show of such profound promise that its cancellation has to rank among the greatest tragedies of all time (among television program cancellations, that is). Though Dan's mental breakdown in the second season was a little abrupt, the show nonetheless was excellent across the board. Writing, acting, even things normally relegated to secondary status such as music, all shone through magnificently in this comedy centered around an upstart network and it's lead sports program. The Simpsons: I can't say enough about this show. For many people my age, Simpsons is THE defining program of our adolescence. Never before have social commentary and comedy blended together so well, and in a format as acceptable as an animated television show. The Simpsons, aside from all it offers on the surface, is a satirical onion. You can peel away layer after layer to reach new depths of appreciation, exceeding even that which was originally intended. Countless expressions, including the immortal D'oh have found their way into our everyday vocabulary, and the stereotypical characters form the basis for many a comparison to participants of our own lives. Of the show, I have really only two complaints, and both of them are recent. Lately, whether the result of intellectual exhaustion or simple laziness, the show has been flagging. The last few seasons were largely forgettable, and though FOX seems content to buy seasons until the heat death of the Universe, I think it would be better if it took its final bow. My other problem with the show is that, ever since the 2000 election, it has been increasingly partisan. The Simpsons always took aim at people from both sides, though the conservative position took more flak (deservedly so too, in my opinion), at least the left got its share of whacks. Aside from the fact that cutting out the left abandons a lot of good material, in some sense the Simpsons are an institution, one that cheapens its legacy by becoming increasingly antagonistic with a particular world view. Sci-Fi Brimstone: The best single season of television ever produced in the English speaking world. Or at least, it's up there.

These include protection against I/R injury in skeletal muscle [18] and liver [19], inhibition of platelet aggregation [20], attenuation of inflammation [21], and enhancement of wound healing [22]. Most importantly, iNO has been shown to prevent and reduce myocardial injury following ischemia/reperfusion in numerous experimental models, both in vivo [23-28] and ex vivo [29-32]. The primary aim of our study was to determine whether iNO can exert direct cardioprotective effects during reperfusion and if so, whether this effect involves activation of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP). We therefore investigated the effects of iNO on myocardial function and infarct size in isolated mouse hearts subjected to global ischemia followed by reperfusion. To test the hypothesis that the mPTP is a key mediator of iNO-induced cardioprotection we then examined the effects of two different mPTP inhibitors, cyclosporine A and bongkrekic acid, on myocardial function and infarct size. All experiments were performed in accordance with the National Institutes of Health Guidelines for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee at Columbia University Medical Center. Male C57BL/6 mice (Charles River Laboratories, Wilmington, MA) weighing 25-30 g were housed under standard conditions (12 h light-dark cycle, 24 C, 60% humidity) and given free access to food and water. Mice were allowed to acclimate to their new environment for at least 72 h prior to experimentation. Isolated working heart preparation Hearts were excised from mice anesthetized with pentobarbital (50 mg/kg i.p.) and placed in ice-cold Krebs-Henseleit solution (KHS: NaCl 118 mM, KCl 4.75 mM, CaCl {2} 1.88 mM, MgSO {4} 1.18 mM, KH {2} PO {4} 1.18 mM, glucose 11 mM, NaHCO {3} 25 mM, pH 7.40 at 37 C). Hearts were perfused retrogradely through the aorta with oxygenated (95% O {2}, 5% CO {2} ) KHS containing 0.01% (w/v) bovine serum albumin (BSA) via a cannula inserted into the ascending aorta. After removal of excess connective tissue, atria and great vessels, the apex of the heart was cannulated and connected to a constant-flow Langendorff apparatus where the heart was perfused with oxygenated KHS at a constant flow rate of 10 ml/min (Harvard Apparatus, Holliston, MA). A latex balloon was inserted into the left ventricle (LV) via the mitral valve and inflated with water until LV developed pressure (LVDP) reached 80 mmHg. This value was maintained throughout the experiment using a servo pump (SMP 1.1, ADInstruments, Colorado Springs, CO). Heart rate (HR) was measured continuously using a pulse transducer attached to the balloon and recorded with PowerLab software (AD Instruments). Coronary flow (CF) was calculated as the difference between inflow and outflow rates. Hemodynamics were recorded every minute. At the end of the experiment, hearts were frozen in liquid nitrogen-cooled isopentane and stored at -80 C until analysis of infarct size.

We can't stop all suffering, but that doesn't mean that we shouldn't stop any. In today's world of virtually unlimited choices, there are plenty of kind, gentle ways for us to feed, clothe, entertain, and educate ourselves that do not involve killing animals."What about plants?"There is currently no reason to believe that plants experience pain because they are devoid of central nervous systems, nerve endings, and brains. It is theorized that animals are able to feel pain so that they can use it for self-protection purposes. For example, if you touch something hot and feel pain, you will learn from the pain that you should not touch that item in the future. Since plants cannot move from place to place and do not need to learn to avoid certain things, this sensation would be superfluous. From a physiological standpoint, plants are completely different from mammals. Unlike animals' body parts, many perennial plants, fruits, and vegetables can be harvested over and over again without dying. If you are concerned about the impact of vegetable agriculture on the environment, you should know that a vegetarian diet is better for the environment than a meat-based one, since the vast majority of grains and legumes raised today are used as feed for cattle. Rather than eating animals, such as cows, who must consume 16 pounds of vegetation in order to convert them into 1 pound of flesh, you can save many more plantsa lives (and destroy less land) by eating vegetables directly."It's fine for you to believe in animal rights, but why do you try to tell other people what to do?"Everybody is entitled to his or her own opinion, but freedom of thought is not the same thing as freedom of action. You are free to believe whatever you want as long as you don't hurt others. You may believe that animals should be killed, that black people should be enslaved, or that women should be beaten, but you don't always have the right to put your beliefs into practice. The very nature of reform movements is to tell others what to do - don't use humans as slaves, don't sexually harass women, etc.aand all movements initially encounter opposition from people who want to continue to take part in the criticized behavior."Animals don't reason, don't understand rights, and don't always respect our rights, so why should we apply our ideas of morality to them?"An animal's inability to understand and adhere to our rules is as irrelevant as a child's or a person with a developmental disability's inability to do so. Animals are not always able to choose to change their behaviors, but adult human beings have the intelligence and ability to choose between behaviors that hurt others and behaviors that do not hurt others.

She wanders about as if she's carrying the weight of the world on her small shoulders. It aches me to see her frown when she ought to be laughing. The other children find joy in simple things-a game of tag, a funny story, a new toy-but not Annette. No, she seems to derive pleasure only from causing mischief or creating a ruckus, though I can only assume it is her way of seeking attention. I often wonder if there's a shadow lurking in her heart, something she cannot quite grasp, something that makes her feel disconnected from the world around her. Just this week, I caught her trying to solicit pebbles from the yard to toss into the flowing brook-we've had heavy rain lately, and it swells to life like a fairytale river. I implored her not to, warning her of the splinters, the mud, the mess it would make of her dress. But the defiance in her eyes suggested that no warning could penetrate her stubborn heart. Such determination to act against my wishes! I suppose she finds some thrill in it, though it makes me worry-what could possibly be left for a young girl who finds merriment in the chaos she creates? This morning, after the debacle with the oil can and Mrs. Larkins, I watched Annette playing alone in the yard, her shadow dancing upon the grass as if mocking the sunlight-an odd sensation to imagine that something so small could provoke such deep introspection. I wondered if there was something simmering underneath the surface of her mischief, a longing to connect yet an inability to do so. She tossed wildflower petals into the air, and for a brief moment, I thought that perhaps this was her version of happiness-a fleeting reminder of innocence, even amidst her mischief. But no-it was a mere distraction, a facade. I sat down on the porch, sipping my tea, my heart heavy with uncertainty. How often had I watched her from a distance when I ought to be by her side? How many chances have I missed to uncover the root of her rebellion? I have a duty, a deeper calling to mold her spirit, yet my own temper obstructs clarity. I need to find the kind of kindness that allows a troubled heart to feel safe enough to open. As I pondered, a sudden commotion interrupted my thoughts-a loud crash followed by an ominous silence. Laura, the neighbor's cat, had darted past like a streak of lightning, embroiled in a temperament more chaotic than mischievous Annette. I hurried to determine the source of the disturbance, half-hoping that it did not lead back to my wild child. Much to my dismay, I discovered broken flower pots scattered across Mrs. Larkins' porch, remnants of Annette's latest 'adventure.' There she was, with dirt smeared on her cheeks and an expression of sheer surprise, as though she had discovered a portal to another world-one where chaotic delight was the law of the land and consequences were mere whispers. "Why, Annette!" I exclaimed incredulously, casting an expectant glance toward the horizon of her feigned innocence. "What on earth possessed you to create such a frightful mess?!"

On the contrary, WMS produces random sequences scattered throughout the genomes, which brings a challenge for correct binning due to lack of universal phylogenetic markers [20]. However, WMS provides much more information about the genetic content of the samples and therefore enables reconstruction of metabolic pathways, identification of horizontally transferred genes or functional characterization of newly discovered species [21]. The binning strategies for WMS data are generally divided into two main categories: similarity-based and composition-based methods. Similarity-based methods use BLAST-like algorithms to compare the sequences against reference databases of known sequences [22,23] and thus require good coverage of the database to achieve accurate results. Composition-based methods exploit the fact that each organism has unique nucleotide distribution pattern along its DNA sequence, called oligonucleotide frequency [24]. These patterns are often represented by tetranucleotides and can be visualized using self-organizing maps (SOM), where similar genomes are clustered together and can be easily distinguished [25]. As composition-based methods do not rely on any reference database, they are able to classify even unknown species. Although many tools were designed to deal with binning problem, none of them achieved sufficient accuracy and reliability at the same time. Therefore, the need for development of new methods still persists. In our work we present a method for binning of metagenomic sequences using artificial neural networks. We show that our method achieves better performance in terms of precision and recall when compared to other state-of-the-art methods. The data set used in our experiments consisted of three metagenomes downloaded from NCBI Sequence Read Archive (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra). Each metagenome contained approximately 50 million reads obtained from Illumina platform and originated from different habitats (Table 1 ). Prior to the training and testing of the model, the data sets had to be processed in order to obtain ground truth labels for individual reads. First, all reads were mapped to the complete bacterial genomes from RefSeq database using Bowtie 2 aligner [26]. Reads mapping to multiple locations or having low alignment score (<30) were discarded. After that, the remaining reads were classified according to their origin and binned accordingly. Since the read length was limited to 100bp, the maximum allowed distance between consecutive reads originating from the same genome was set to 500bp to minimize false positive assignments. To train the model, we selected 150 bacterial genomes covering all phyla present in the data set. For each of the genomes, 3000 sequences of 100bp were randomly generated using wgsim software [27]. Subsequently, all generated sequences were combined and shuffled to form a single file. The final training set contained 450 000 sequences. Next, another 150 genomes were chosen to create validation and test sets. From each genome, 6000 sequences were extracted in the same way as described above, resulting in 900 000 sequences per set. The validation set was used during the training phase to evaluate the performance of the model and decide whether to continue learning or stop if the error rate increased. The test set served for the final evaluation of the trained model after the learning phase ended. All data processing steps including binning and generation of training, validation and test sets were performed using custom Python scripts. The code is available upon request. Model architecture Our method utilizes artificial neural network for binning of short metagenomic sequences. It consists of two main components: feature extraction and classification. The former component takes a sequence as input and converts it into numerical vector, whereas the latter predicts the class label based on the vector representation of the sequence. Both components are implemented as separate models and described below.

If you fall under the spell of your sexual attraction immediately, you need to look beyond it for other keys to compatibility. One of these is laughter. Laughter tells you how much you will enjoy each others company over the long term. If your laughter together is good and healthy, and not at the expense of others, then you have a healthy relationship to the world. Laughter is the child of surprise. If you can make each other laugh, you can always surprise each other. And if you can always surprise each other, you can always keep the world around you new. Beware of a relationship in which there is no laughter. Even the most intimate relationships based only on seriousness have a tendency to turn sour. Over time, sharing a common serious viewpoint on the world tends to turn you against those who do not share the same viewpoint, and your relationship can become based on being critical together. After laughter, look for a partner who deals with the world in a way you respect. When two people first get together, they tend to see their relationship as existing only in the space between the two of them. They find each other endlessly fascinating, and the overwhelming power of the emotions they are sharing obscures the outside world. As the relationship ages and grows, the outside world becomes important again. If your partner treats people or circumstances in a way you can't accept, you will inevitably come to grief.Look at the way she cares for others and deals with the daily affairs of life. If that makes you love her more, your love will grow. If it does not, be careful. If you do not respect the way you each deal with the world around you, eventually the two of you will not respect each other. Look also at how your partner confronts the mysteries of life.

However, modern physics has revealed a far more complex and counterintuitive reality, where the principles of quantum mechanics and relativity govern the behavior of matter and energy. This realization should humble our confidence in our understanding of the physical world and make us more cautious in assuming that we can reduce the workings of the mind to purely physical processes. Furthermore, even if we grant that the physical world is governed by deterministic laws, it's unclear how these laws can account for the subjective, qualitative aspects of conscious experience. The so-called "hard problem" of consciousness, famously formulated by philosopher David Chalmers, questions why we have subjective experiences at all. Why do we experience the world in the way that we do, rather than just processing information in a more mechanical or computational manner? Materialism, or physicalism, seems ill-equipped to provide a satisfactory answer to this question. It's difficult to see how the aggregation of physical particles and processes could give rise to the rich, subjective experience that we call consciousness. The materialist might respond by positing that consciousness is an emergent property of complex systems, but this merely pushes the question back a step: what exactly is it about complex systems that gives rise to consciousness? In addition, the materialist perspective struggles to account for the intentionality of mental states, or their ability to be directed towards objects and aspects of the world. Our thoughts and feelings are not just internal states, but are inherently directed towards things outside of ourselves. This intentionality is difficult to reconcile with a purely physical understanding of the mind, which would seem to reduce mental states to mere internal processes. Finally, the materialist view of the mind-body problem raises questions about the nature of personal identity and free will. If the mind is simply a product of physical processes, do we really have control over our thoughts and actions, or are they determined by prior causes? And what does it mean to be a person, if our mental states are simply the result of physical processes in the brain? In light of these difficulties, it's worth reconsidering the dualist perspective, despite its own set of challenges. Perhaps the mind is not simply a product of the physical world, but a distinct entity that interacts with the body in complex ways. This view may be less fashionable in modern philosophical circles, but it remains a viable option for those who are unsatisfied with the limitations of materialism. Ultimately, the mind-body problem remains one of the most fundamental and intractable puzzles of philosophy, and it's unlikely that a single solution will be found anytime soon. However, by carefully considering the strengths and weaknesses of different perspectives, we can continue to deepen our understanding of this complex and multifaceted issue.

'You'd better come along, then,' returned her brother, holding out his hand. 'We're going home to breakfast.' 'I'm afraid we haven't got many eggs,' said Tricksy regretfully. 'The others have taken them all. You'll get into a row, Dods.' 'Can't help that,' replied her brother cheerily. 'They didn't leave me much chance. Come along!' He helped his little sister over the rough places, and they walked across the moor together till they reached the edge of a ravine which divided the moorland from the shore. Here a number of people were assembled, some with pails of milk in their hands, others carrying baskets of eggs. There were men and women, boys and girls, and two or three babies, all chattering and laughing merrily, except the babies, who were fast asleep. They had just come ashore after spending the night in fishing boats, and were preparing to return to their homes, scattered here and there among the rocks and heather. In the midst of the group stood a tall, bony woman, with sharp features and keen grey eyes, which seemed to take in everything at once. She wore a blue print gown and a red shawl crossed over her breast, and held in her arms a baby wrapped in flannel petticoats and shawls. She was talking volubly to a young fisherman, who listened respectfully, although he did not seem quite pleased about something. 'What d'ye mean by letting yon lads beat ye to the cliff, Davie?' she exclaimed sharply. 'Ye should ha' been there before them! What for did ye let them pass ye? Ye'll be losing your job if ye dinna look sharp!' 'I canna help it, Mrs Macdonald,' answered the man sullenly. 'That's what comes o' being late away last nicht. It's a' verra fine tae talk aboot getting up at four o'clock in the morning; but when we were nae sooner doon than it was time tae start back, it would ha' been mair sensible tae stay where we were. We wad ha' made better speed wi' the tide behind us.' 'Nonsense, man!' retorted Mrs Macdonald contemptuously. 'A bit o' wind in your face will never hurt you. And what for did ye waste your time drinking in the village yesterday afternoon instead o' coming straight hame?' 'It's my business what I dae wi' my time,' growled the man angrily. 'If I choose to spend my money i' the public-house, what is that tae you?' 'It's a great deal to me, and to everybody else!' snapped the woman. 'When a man drinks more than he can carry, he disgraces his family, and brings shame upon decent folk. If ye want to drink, do it quietly, like other folk, and dinna make a show o' yourself before strangers.' 'Strangers indeed!' cried the man, growing redder in the face. 'There are nae strangers in Erisaig. Everybody kens everybody else's business.' 'And a good thing too!' declared Mrs Macdonald emphatically. 'If there were fewer secrets and less deceit, there would be fewer scandals and broken hearts. But that's neither here nor there. What I say is this: if ye expect tae keep your place as skipper o' my boat, ye maun behave yourself properly, and give satisfaction. Do ye hear?'

This exclamation was caused by the appearance of a bright point of light on the edge of the bluff, several hundred yards down the river, and upon the opposite side. At first glance it resembled some star of the first magnitude, which a sudden depression of the bluff had made visible. The scout ceased paddling, and, suffering the canoe to drift slowly with the tide, fixed his keen gray eyes upon the fiery point. "That ain't any more of a star than I am," he added, a second later. "There she goes again!" The torch, for such it was, remained stationary for scarcely a minute, when it began revolving swiftly from right to left, the gyration being of such a nature as to prove that it was swung by the hand of some person. Three revolutions, and then it suddenly reversed and made three in the opposite direction, then two back, then two forward, then one back and forth, and then it vanished in the gloom of the night. Tom scarcely breathed while viewing this pantomime, and when it ended he still held the paddle motionless while he chuckled to himself, for he knew what it all meant. He had seen Indian telegraphy before, and had learned to comprehend a great deal of those mysterious signs and signals by which news is carried across mountain and prairie with incredible speed. He had ridden his fleet mustang to death to head off some of these telegrams, and yet in every case the Indians, by some trickery unexplained to him, had outsped him. "Yes, I can read that," Tom growled, still drifting with the current. "That ere redskin is signalin' to some other scamp, and it's all about me. It says that I'm on the river somewhere, and a lookout must be kept for me." Such was the fact. The Indian who swayed the torch meant thereby to appraise some confederate that the scout who had dared to penetrate such a distance into their country, and to unearth their most important secrets, was seeking to make his way down the Rio Gila and out of their country again. This much said the torch in language that could not be mistaken. Although it added no more, yet the sequence was inevitable, and Tom needed no one to apprise him that the river both above and below him was closely watched, and that he was in the greatest peril of his life. By doing so, they effectively mitigate the sharp transitions that can lead to the steepening of pressure waves, attenuating their potential for generating significant external disturbances. Engineering these structures requires a nuanced understanding of fluid dynamics and sound propagation principles, ensuring that the solutions deployed are optimized for both effectiveness and aesthetic integration into the landscape. The design of transition areas can take various forms, from gradual slopes that allow smoother airflow encroachments to the incorporation of complex geometries that induce turbulence and thereby dissipate wave energy more effectively. These approaches not only seek to minimize disturbances but also often aim to enhance the visual appeal of the tunnel entrance, which can be especially critical in urban settings. The integration of vegetation or artistic elements alongside these structures can turn functional engineering challenges into opportunities for public engagement and community acceptance [7]. Furthermore, it's essential to understand the role of materials in this context. The choice of construction materials can significantly influence a transition area's efficacy. Soft, porous materials might absorb sound and reduce reverberations, while harder, reflective surfaces can redirect waves away from sensitive zones. Thus, an interdisciplinary approach, blending acoustics, engineering principles, and landscape design, often yields the best results. High-speed rail systems, which necessitate regular use of tunnels, are in many ways at the forefront of this challenge. Considerations extend beyond the immediate pressures and noises-they encompass the broader implications of construction and operational zones. Engineers continuously monitor the interactions between train velocity, tunnel length, and the resultant aerodynamic behaviors. Computational simulations have emerged as an invaluable tool in such studies, enabling designers to predict with greater accuracy how modifications to a tunnel's entrance might influence external disturbances. In addition to designing adequate entrances, advances in technology also provide alternative methods to mitigate MPWs. Active noise control systems, akin to those used in certain industrial applications, suggest that further creative avenues exist. By deploying sensors to detect incoming pressure waves, these systems could trigger counter-wave emissions tuned to cancel out the effects of outgoing disturbances. Such innovations hold the potential for both immediate relief and long-term solutions to the challenges posed by high-speed rail systems. As the demand for rapid transit increases, so too does the necessity to address the implications of high-speed travel on urban landscapes. Through thoughtful design, robust engineering, and continual research, the industry can not only minimize disturbances but also enhance the acceptance of high-speed rail solutions in densely populated areas. However, this equilibrium requires a commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration among engineers, urban planners, and community stakeholders. Their collective insights will be indispensable for developing practical strategies that harmonize the need for efficiency with the obligation to safeguard public welfare. Nevertheless, despite these advances and solutions, the nature of high-speed transit inherently presents ongoing challenges, as each new rail line offers a distinct context for its interactions with tunnels. Thus, a dynamic approach to design, grounded in empirical evidence and supplemented by innovation, remains crucial as we navigate the evolving landscape of transportation infrastructure. Continued research into wave propagation, reflection mechanisms, and environmental impacts will further enhance our understanding and capability to manage the complexities associated with modern rail travel effectively.

When Mr. Hampton decided to go to Texas and New Mexico as the representative of a group of "independent" oil operators engaged in a bitter war with the Oil Trust known as the "Octopus," Jack begged so hard to be permitted to go along that his father let him quit Harrington Hall Military Academy two months before the end of the term. It was agreed that when school ended, June 28, Frank and Bob should join Jack in the Southwest for their summer vacation. The two boys owned an airplane in which they hoped to make the trip when the time came. Mr. Temple, however, was dubious about letting them attempt to make so long a flight alone. "But, Dad," Bob would argue, whenever the matter was discussed, "we'll be all right. We've made lots of flights without any accidents. We're as capable as anybody. Not much older than we are now." It must be confessed that Mrs. Temple thought little of the matter one way or the other. She had so many social duties to take up her time that there was little left for the boys. Accordingly, the boys had only Mr. Temple to persuade and they felt pretty certain of doing that in time. So the last two months of school were spent in poring over maps and routes, and in studying up on landing fields and flying conditions generally throughout the territory they would have to cover. Much of this study for the proposed flight was carried on at the radiophone station on the Hampton estate. Mr. Hampton was an enthusiast about the development of radio telephony and it was through him the boys first had become interested in the subject. A year earlier he had built a powerful station for the purpose of making experiments in talking across the ocean. On that account the United States Government had granted him a special permit to use an 1,800 metre wave length. Before leaving for the Southwest, Jack told the boys his father intended to build in Texas or New Mexico another radiophone station of similar wave length. This would enable Mr. Hampton to communicate with his New York confreres through his Long Island station. The big thing to the boys, however, was that they would be able to talk to each other across 2,000 miles of territory. Delays in construction in the Southwest had occurred, however, and communication between the two stations had not yet been established when our story opens. As the boys re-entered the station after their inspection of the weather, Bob threw himself sprawlingly into a deep wicker chair and, picking up a book, began idly to turn the pages.

At the period of which we write the valley had just been taken possession of by several families of squatters, who, tired of the turmoil and the squabbles of the then frontier settlements, had pushed boldly into the far west to seek a new home for themselves, where they could have "elbow room," regardless alike of the dangers they might encounter in unknown lands and of the Red-skins who dwelt there. The squatters were well armed with axes, rifles, and ammunition. Most of the women were used to dangers and alarms, and placed implicit reliance in the power of their fathers, husbands, and brothers to protect them - and well they might, for a bolder set of stalwart men than these backwoodsmen never trod the wilderness. Each had been trained to the use of the rifle and the axe from infancy, and many of them had spent so much of their lives in the woods, that they were more than a match for the Indian in his own peculiar pursuits of hunting and war. When the squatters first issued from the woods bordering the valley, an immense herd of wild horses or mustangs were browsing on the plain. These no sooner beheld the cavalcade of white men, than, uttering a wild neigh, they tossed their flowing manes in the breeze and dashed away like a whirlwind. This incident procured the valley its name. The newcomers gave one satisfied glance at their future home, and then set to work to erect log huts forthwith. Soon the axe was heard ringing through the forests, and tree after tree fell to the ground, while the occasional sharp ring of a rifle told that the hunters were catering successfully for the camp. In course of time the Mustang Valley began to assume the aspect of a thriving settlement, with cottages and waving fields clustered together in the midst of it. Of course the savages soon found it out, and paid it occasional visits. These dark-skinned tenants of the woods brought furs of wild animals with them, which they exchanged with the white men for knives, and beads, and baubles and trinkets of brass and tin. But they hated the "Pale-faces" with bitter hatred, because their encroachments had at this time materially curtailed the extent of their hunting grounds, and nothing but the numbers and known courage of the squatters prevented these savages from butchering and scalping them all. The leader of this band of pioneers was a Major Hope, a gentleman whose love for nature in its wildest aspects determined him to exchange barrack life for a life in the woods. The major was a first-rate shot, a bold, fearless man, and an enthusiastic naturalist. He was past the prime of life, and, being a bachelor, was unencumbered with a family.

The new EU sanctions will restrict Russian state-owned banks from accessing European capital markets, and stop or slow the export of oil-related equipment and technology to Russia. They also will stop new contracts for arms imports and exports between the European Union and Russia, and prohibit the export of goods and technology that can be used for both military and civilian purposes. "It is meant as a strong warning: Illegal annexation of territory and deliberate destabilization of a neighboring sovereign country cannot be accepted in 21st century Europe," the EU said in a statement. To punish Russia, Europe must be prepared to suffer. What Obama announced. Two hours later, Obama told reporters that the United States expanded its July 16 sanctions to include three more state-owned banks and another weapons company, while also targeting technology for deep-water, Arctic and shale oil production. While expanding on the earlier moves, the latest sanctions include limits. They don't affect Russia's current oil production, instead targeting the ability to develop new areas, senior administration officials told reporters on a background call. The European sanctions on weapons trade only involves future transactions, allowing France to complete an existing helicopter deal with Moscow. However, Obama cited the joint action as significant, saying that "because we are closely coordinating our actions with Europe, the sanctions we are announcing today will have an even bigger bite." "If Russia continues on its current path, the cost on Russia will continue to grow," he added, calling the moves "a reminder that the United States means what it says, and we will rally the international community in standing up for the rights and freedom of people around the world." What is the impact? The senior administration officials said the expanded sanctions prevent Russia's state-owned banks, which have all or most of their debt in U.S. dollars, from getting more medium- and long-term financing in America. They noted the sanctions already have contributed to a downturn in the Russian economy, a flight of foreign capital and weakening of the ruble currency. "Russia is not a very good bet right now for international investors," one of the officials said. On Tuesday, shares in British oil giant BP fell by 2.5% after the company warned that it would suffer from the tougher EU sanctions. BP owns a significant stake in Rosneft, Russia's biggest oil company, which no longer can access long-term financing from U.S. sources. Meanwhile, shares in French automotive manufacturer Renault slumped by 4.5% as the company warned about a sharp slowdown in emerging markets, including Russia. Russia is Renault's third largest market, based on sales. Geopolitically, Obama denied that a new Cold War with Russia had started, but the head of the foreign affairs committee in Russia's State Duma - the lower house of parliament - disagreed. Aleksey Pushkov tweeted Wednesday that Obama will make history as "the statesman who started a new Cold War."

The advancements in CPCs represent a crucial step forward, yet the landscape of solar energy innovation is multifaceted and ever-evolving. Alongside experimental solutions, theoretical research and simulation efforts are paramount in deciphering the complex interactions between light and materials, enabling precise modeling and optimization. Theoretical research delves into the fundamental principles governing photovoltaic efficiency, exploring the potential of novel semiconductor materials and multi-junction cells that promise to significantly boost conversion rates. As researchers unravel the quantum mechanics and thermodynamic limitations shackling solar technology, breakthroughs in material science continue to drive progress. Simulation, as the third research thrust, employs sophisticated computational models to predict the behavior of solar devices under various conditions. By simulating different environmental conditions and material configurations, scientists are able to forecast the performance and longevity of solar systems, thus guiding practical applications and informing cost-effective manufacturing processes. These simulations help in creating highly detailed digital twins of physical structures, optimizing designs before they transition into reality. In synergy with experimental findings, simulations refine energy capture methods, informing the placement and orientation of solar panels to harness the maximum possible sunlight. Yet, challenges remain formidable. Environmental factors such as dust, shading, and weather changes pose substantial hurdles, affecting the energy yield and long-term reliability of solar installations. Research is, therefore, directed towards devising adaptive systems capable of mitigating these impediments, advocating for intelligent mechanisms that self-clean and recover energy losses. Amid these technological strides, an essential focus is on the sustainability and lifecycle of materials used in solar technologies. The ecological impact of production and disposal processes must be minimized to truly uphold the promise of green energy. Scientists strive to substitute rare, non-renewable resources with abundant, eco-friendly alternatives that do not compromise efficiency or durability. In parallel, policy and economic frameworks must evolve to support these innovations. Governments and industry stakeholders are called upon to invest in infrastructure, incentivize research and development, and facilitate the integration of solar technologies into the broader energy grid. Such systemic efforts are crucial for the rapid scaling and widespread adoption of solar solutions, ensuring they stand as viable alternatives to fossil fuels. Moreover, public awareness and community engagement play vital roles in this transition. Educating communities about the benefits of solar energy not only fosters acceptance but also galvanizes collective action towards a sustainable future. Pilot projects, subsidy programs, and educational initiatives are instrumental in cultivating an informed society that values and actively participates in the advancement of renewable energy. As the journey to harness the sun's power continues, the confluence of experimental, theoretical, and simulation research holds promise. Converting untapped solar potential into practical reality demands an interdisciplinary approach powered by collaboration, innovation, and unwavering commitment. By navigating the challenges of cost, efficiency, and environmental impact, solar energy endeavors to eclipse its nascent stages and emerge as a cornerstone of global energy solutions. As research pioneers chart new territories, each discovery inches the world closer to a horizon where solar energy is not just a supplement, but a primary pillar of sustainable living.

The first two studies identified neighboring producers based on a given kilometre grid-square level and the municipality centroid, respectively, while the last study was the only one that had access to exact geographical coordinates (i.e. latitude and longitude). All the above studies reported a positive dependence in neighboring producers' efficiency scores. However, the present study argues that irrespective of the scale considered, the spatial autoregressive efficiency model employed by the above studies raises some theoretical as well as methodological challenges. Theoretically-wise, the aforementioned studies assume that individuals' efficiency is only related to their neighbors' efficiency and an error component, which is somewhat restrictive as one would expect that it would also be influenced by individuals' characteristics (i.e. subsidies received, management practices etc.). More importantly, neglecting these characteristics raises a methodological issue as it does not allow the above studies to perform the required inference and make statements regarding the nature and magnitude of spatial spillovers. According to Anselin (1988), LeSage and Pace (2009) and Elhorst (2014), inference in a spatial autoregressive model is not directly based on the parameter associated with the neighbors' dependent variable (in this case neighbors' efficiency), but on the derivation of the so-called direct and indirect marginal effects of the utilized firm characteristics. The direct effect measures the change in individuals' technical efficiency as a result of a change in one of their own characteristics, while the indirect effect quantifies the change in individuals' technical efficiency due to a change in one of their neighbors' characteristics. Therefore, the derivation of indirect effects allows one to make statements regarding the type and magnitude of spatial spillovers. For instance, if an increase in neighboring producers' experience contributes to an increase in individuals' efficiency, this implies that neighboring producers may indeed communicate and share their knowledge and experience, which ultimately leads to the individuals' efficiency gains. Finally, all the aforementioned spatial efficiency studies disregarded the presence of endogeneity in the spatial autoregressive model, which may result in biased estimates (LeSage & Pace, 2009). Endogeneity exists due to simultaneity as the dependent variable of any individual appears both on left and the right-hand side of the spatial autoregressive model. This study adds to the literature that explores the existence of spatial dependence in producers' efficiency. Although it is interesting to merely study whether producers' efficiency levels are spatially dependent, it is more informative to know the nature and magnitude of spatial spillovers. If, for instance, empirical evidence shows that spatial spillovers exist because producers communicate with each other, policy-makers can take advantage of this information domino effect and promote more efficiently new technologies that can improve producers' performance. Specifically, this study contributes to the literature in four ways. First, it uses a farm-level panel dataset that contains information on the exact geographical location of farms based on their latitude and longitude.

Moreover, the integration of oxy-fuel combustion technology with fluidized bed systems presents a unique opportunity to transcend conventional energy paradigms while addressing the pressing challenges posed by climate change. The flexibility inherent in fluidized bed combustion (FBC) not only accommodates a variety of fuels-including biomass and waste materials-but also provides an ideal platform for the adaptation of oxy-fuel processes. The capability to utilize diverse feedstocks aligns seamlessly with global sustainability goals, heralding a shift towards more responsible energy consumption. In this context, the combustion environment of fluidized beds enhances the gas-solid interaction, thereby ensuring improved burn-out characteristics. The lower particle agglomeration and higher heat transfer rates achieved through fluidization can significantly optimize the combustion efficiency. Furthermore, the potential for higher combustion efficiency is underscored by the ability of FBC to operate at lower temperatures, which is essential for controlling the formation of nitrogen oxides (NOx). This is an essential factor, considering the evolving legislative frameworks that call for stringent emission controls. The advancements in oxy-fuel combustion technology also pave the way for innovative carbon capture methodologies. Capturing CO2 as a result of higher purity emissions not only eases the separation process but enhances the viability of carbon dioxide sequestration or utilization strategies. The adoption of this approach could foster a circular carbon economy, wherein captured CO2 is potentially utilized for enhanced oil recovery or converted into useful products such as fuels or feedstock in the chemical industry. Thus, the integration of carbon capture technologies with renewable energy sources redefines the role of fossil fuels and positions biomass as a cornerstone in the transition to a sustainable energy landscape. Furthermore, the deployment of intelligent control systems alongside oxy-fuel fluidized bed technologies can unlock new realms of operational efficiency. With real-time monitoring and data analytics, power plants can optimize their combustion processes, minimizing waste and maximizing output. This trend towards digitization in the energy sector signifies a paradigm shift, transforming traditional practices into smart, responsive systems that are capable of adapting to fluctuations in supply and demand. It is essential, however, to recognize the socioeconomic dimensions of transitioning to advanced combustion technologies. The successful deployment of BECCS and oxy-fuel fluidized bed systems hinges not only on technical feasibility but also on societal acceptance, regulatory frameworks, and economic incentives. Policymakers must facilitate the development and dissemination of these technologies through supportive legislation, while fostering engagement with communities to address concerns related to land use, biomass sourcing, and potential impacts on local ecosystems. Investment in research and development remains a crucial component in driving innovation forward. Collaborative efforts among academia, industry, and governmental bodies can catalyze breakthroughs in technologies that could further enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of carbon capture and storage solutions. The pathway to a low-carbon future is undoubtedly fraught with challenges. Nonetheless, the concerted strides towards the integration of oxy-fuel combustion with fluidized bed technology mark a pivotal step in transforming the energy landscape. The dual benefits of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and harnessing renewable energy sources converge, reflecting a proactive response to the existential threats posed by climate change. It is with this vision that stakeholders across sectors must unite, pushing the boundaries of what is achievable and ensuring a sustainable environment for generations to come. The choices made today will echo in the landscapes of tomorrow, compelling a thorough reassessment of our energy portfolio and an unwavering commitment to innovations that champion sustainability.

Analysing the "efficiency gap", the lack of reliable information on carbon mitigation measures is identified as a key reason for the gap [10,16]. So there is a real need for robust and openly accessible knowledge on which to base high-level assessments. This study seeks to address the existing 'knowledge gap' in relation to the potential of wind power technology. A few studies have considered the fuel savings potential of wind power technologies analysing wind data from weather models along certain shipping lanes. In particular, Clauss et al. [17] use data from the ERA-40 database, with a resolution of 2.5 * 2.5 from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), to calculate fuel savings from five different sail types on three different routes. Acknowledging strong simplifications in their study, they conclude that significant savings of up to 15% at a speed of 15 knots and up to 44% at 10 knots can be made for some of the analysed ship types. They suggest the technology is cost-effective, given rising fuel costs and environmental pressures, and argue the need for more detailed analyses. Schlaak et al. [18] incorporate results from field trials with a kite into a study of the potential contribution on a network of 15 global shipping routes, using the same database. Significant fuel saving potential for a multi-purpose freighter, between 1% and 21% for a ship speed of 15 knots and between 4% and 36% for a ship speed of 13 knots, is shown. Due to time-averaging of wind speed data, they consider the result as a first order estimate. On a similar tack, this paper introduces a numerical performance model of a Flettner rotor and one of a towing kite. They are combined with wind data from the Met Office's Unified Model with a high spatial resolution of less than 1. A methodology for assessing the wind power contribution of the technologies towards ship propulsion is provided and applied to five different shipping routes, representing different trades, served by ships of different types and size, in different environmental conditions. In relation to the existing literature, in particular [17,18], the wind speed data used in the present paper have a higher spatial and temporal resolution. In terms of technology options, Clauss et al. [17] study various sail types, and Schlaak et al. [18] analyse a towing kite. While this study contributes to the literature by presenting a technology model of a Flettner model, the modularity of the technology model, and the inclusion of the model of a towing kite in particular, allow for the comparison of wind power technologies with different properties that operate on different mechanisms. Furthermore, the methodology stresses simplicity and modularity, high-lighting potential power savings, rather than scoping percentage savings that depend strongly on external parameters such as ship size and type.
