Batch trajectories with variable lengths can also be synchronized through appropriately translating, expanding and contracting localized segments within them. Typical methodologies for such kind of synchronization include Correlation Optimized Warping (COW) and Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) [9]. Their ability to align chromatographic and spectroscopic profiles were further compared in [17,18]. COW approach was originally designed to correct peak shifts in chromatographic profiles [19] and it has some limitations for baseline corrections although the correlation coefficient offers a better similarity measurement. The application of COW in on-line batch process monitoring can be found in [20]. DTW approach, which was extensively developed in speech recognition to match similar events between signals, has a wider application in the synchronization of batch trajectories. DTW uses the principle of dynamic programming to minimize a dissimilarity measurement or a distance between two trajectories and it may shift some feature vectors in time, compress some and/or expand others so that a minimum distance is achieved [21]. DTW was first introduced into chemometrics as a tool for supervision and fault detection with particular reference to bioprocess applications [22]. Then Kassidas et al. [2] adapted the DTW algorithm to batch statistical process control as a tool to synchronize batches with different lengths and/or different local times. Thereafter various modified versions of DTW were proposed in the literature for batch trajectory synchronization [23,24,9]. For example, a robust DTW algorithm was proposed in [23] through combining a moving window least squares procedure with derivative DTW so as to avoid singularity points and reduce the bias of alignment results towards the reference trajectory. Most recently, an adaptation from Kassidas et al.'s approach was introduced in [9] to achieve on-line synchronization of batch trajectories. Given any two trajectories with different lengths, DTW can be applied to synchronize them as there is always an optimal solution to minimize the distance between these two trajectories according to certain criteria. Such a synchronization mechanism considers little about the process dynamics. As a result, DTW may distort the inherent process dynamics during the adjustment of localized segments and thus the ability for fault detection and diagnosis using the synchronized data can be reduced in some occasions [25]. Except for the synchronization of process variable trajectories, the batch end-product quality measured at the end of batch runs needs to be aligned as well due to the change of batch durations for shorter batches after the synchronization. For the indicator variable approach or the DTW approach, the future batch end-product quality at the synchronized batch duration time for those shorter batches can simply be assumed to be the same values at their original endpoints. However, this may not be true due to the change of batch durations for those shorter batches, especially in case of a large change of batch durations. An alternative approach is to predict the future batch end-product quality values at the synchronized batch duration time for shorter batches using a pre-determined model.

The heat pipe heat exchanger's ability to transport large amounts of heat without moving parts makes it an attractive solution for waste heat recovery applications in the steel industry. However, the presence of contaminants and fouling in the exhaust gases can significantly impact the thermal performance of the HPHE. Fouling can reduce the heat transfer efficiency by up to 30% [10]. Therefore, it is essential to develop effective cleaning methods to maintain the HPHE's performance. Several studies have investigated the use of different cleaning methods to remove fouling deposits from HPHEs. One common method is the use of chemical cleaning agents, which can be effective in removing organic fouling deposits [11]. However, chemical cleaning agents can be corrosive and may damage the heat pipe's inner surface. Another method is the use of mechanical cleaning methods, such as brushing or scrubbing, which can be effective in removing inorganic fouling deposits [12]. However, mechanical cleaning methods can be labor-intensive and may not be suitable for large-scale applications. In recent years, researchers have been exploring the use of advanced cleaning technologies, such as plasma cleaning and ultrasonic cleaning, to remove fouling deposits from HPHEs [13, 14]. These technologies have shown promising results in removing fouling deposits without damaging the heat pipe's inner surface. In addition to cleaning methods, researchers have also been investigating the use of coatings and surface treatments to reduce fouling and improve the thermal performance of HPHEs. One common coating material used is titanium dioxide (TiO2), which has been shown to have excellent anti-fouling properties [15]. Another coating material being researched is graphene, which has been shown to have excellent thermal conductivity and anti-fouling properties [16]. In conclusion, waste heat recovery is a crucial aspect of the steel industry's efforts to reduce its environmental impact. Heat pipe heat exchangers are an attractive solution for waste heat recovery due to their ability to transport large amounts of heat without moving parts. However, the presence of contaminants and fouling in the exhaust gases can significantly impact the thermal performance of the HPHE. Effective cleaning methods and advanced technologies, such as plasma cleaning and ultrasonic cleaning, are being researched to maintain the HPHE's performance. Additionally, coatings and surface treatments, such as TiO2 and graphene, are being explored to reduce fouling and improve the thermal performance of HPHEs. Further research is needed to develop effective and efficient cleaning methods and coatings for HPHEs to ensure their widespread adoption in the steel industry. This picture says that physicists have broken down the world into smaller and smaller pieces (down to the sub-atomic level) and have analyzed the forces and relations among these particles. Then, knowing the position and relations of these particles, you can predict the future course of the system. Actually, you can't. For one thing, you run into the conceptual problems of quantum physics at the sub-atomic level. Most people have heard of quantum physics and may know something about it, but I don't think it has penetrated into our everyday thinking. In the twentieth century, physicists overthrew the billiard ball world with the development of quantum mechanics and general relativity. In the case of quantum mechanics, the mathematics which best describe phenomena at the sub-atomic level have mysterious implications for the nature of reality. One finds that you can't pinpoint the position as well as the momentum of a particle through observation (the uncertainty principle). Also, sub-atomic entities can exhibit the character of both particles and waves. Finally, in some circumstances particles seem to be able to act on each other instantaneously at a distance. While I won't try to discuss the details of modern physics here, I just want to make the point that in considering how to address the mind/body problem there is arguably as much mystery remaining in the ultimate nature of matter and energy a the body side of the problem - as there is in addressing the nature of mind. However, at this stage I want to discuss directly why science has a particularly hard time explaining mind or consciousness. Also, this will set the stage for me to put forward a solution to the mind/body mystery. The reason for the difficulty lies in the scientific method itself. Each of us has a unique and subjective point of view. Furthermore, our perspective on the universe comes from a vantage point within the universe. No person can claim to have a perfectly objective view, since this would require a god-like perspective coming from outside the universe. The power of the scientific approach is that one simulates objectivity. This is done by carefully examining things using methods which lead to repeatable results which can be validated by other people. This is very powerful and is the basis of the great success of science. Now, pretend you are a scientist examining my consciousness. You would probably look at my brain very carefully. You would compare what is happening to my neurons and brain chemistry with what is going on with my behavior and my verbal reports about what I'm experiencing. When you are done, you will potentially have explained a great deal about my mind, but one thing will be left over: you will not learn what it is like to have my first person experience a to feel what it is like to be me afrom the insidea. Let me try to pin down what I mean.

Soft drugs are locally active, in this case in the skin, but then undergo rapid systemic metabolism, to metabolites, which are either inactive or rapidly cleared from the systemic circulation.18 Esters can be metabolised in liver by esterases and cytochrome P450 enzymes.19 However, most tissues are capable of metabolising an ester. Importantly, human blood contains a wide range of esterases and the rate of ester hydrolysis in blood can lead to ultra-rapid clearance,20 what we term a super-soft drug. Because S1PR agonists induce transient bradycardia, and as blood returning to circulation from skin passes through the heart before reaching the liver, we felt that a very rapid blood clearance mechanism could potentially discharge the cardiotoxicity risk. To select compounds which would be likely to demonstrate the desired pharmacokinetic profile, we targeted a human plasma stability half-life of 7 and a logP in the range of 2-4 which is believed to be optimal for skin penetration.21 Compounds 4a and 5a-d were synthesised as shown in Scheme 1. The core 2 was synthesised utilising a one-pot, two step reaction. Only the Z isomer was observed. N-propylamine was reacted with 1-isothiocyanato-2-methylbenzene 1 to give the resulting thiourea, which was condensed with 2-bromoacetyl bromide followed by addition of pyridine to furnish the desired thiazolidin-4-one 2. This core was then condensed with the appropriately substituted benzaldehyde 3a-b to furnish 4a and 5a. Finally, esterification or amidation of 4a gave the desired products. Based on the configurational analysis by X-ray, which characterised crystalline analogues of ponesimod as Z,Z22, all structurally related compounds 4a, 5a-d, 11, 12a-f and 15a, b were assigned to the Z,Z-isomer. We selected human plasma stability as a model for human blood metabolism. Esters 5a-c and amide 5d demonstrated half-lives of >180 min in human plasma, far greater than the -Arrestin recruitment assay.23 All of the ester and amide compounds in Table 1 were active and had pIC50 values ranging from 6.5 to 7.0, with the exception of compound 5a where a chlorine ortho to the ester provided 100-fold improvement in activity compared to 5b. Gratifyingly, the parent carboxylic acid 4a, which is the desired metabolite of our esters/amides was less active, giving a pIC50 of <6 and meeting our targeted criteria for producing inactive metabolites. Aqueous solubility is an important parameter for topically applied drugs. Increasing aqueous solubility, should directly increase skin penetration rates.24 Increasing aqueous solubility also increases the range of formulation options that can be used in pre-clinical development.

But you look like an honest man, and if you will come with me to my cottage, I will help you as far as I can to-morrow morning." "Thank you," said the traveller. "I accept your offer." "Well then, I have just made my last stroke," said the old man, lifting up his axe. "We will load our asses and be off. We have some way to go, as I live farther up the valley of Gutech, and even I prefer daylight to darkness for travelling these wild paths. If you had not found me I cannot say when you would have got out of the forest." Without further waste of words, the old man and young Karl set to work to load the asses, strapping on the huge fagots with thongs of leather, while the patient animals, putting out their fore-legs, quietly endured all the tugs and pulls to which they were subjected. "That pack of yours seems heavy, friend traveller," said the old man, glancing at his companion; "let me carry it for you." "No, no! Thanks to you," answered the traveller. "I am strong and hearty. I would not put that on your shoulders which I feel burdensome to my own." "Then let us put it on the back of one of the asses," said the woodcutter; "it will make but little difference to our long-eared friend." "A merciful man is merciful to his beast," said the traveller. "The poor brutes seem already somewhat overloaded, and I should be unwilling to add to their pain for the sake of relieving myself." "Then let Karl, there, carry it; he is sturdy, and can bear it some little way, at all events," said the old man. "I would not place on young shoulders what I find tire a well-knit pair," said the traveller, glancing at young Karl. "But perhaps he may like to get some of the contents of my pack inside his head," he added. "Down his mouth, I suppose you mean," said the old man, laughing. "Is it food or liquor you carry in your pack?" "No, indeed, friend," answered the traveller. "Yet it is food, of a sort food for the mind, and better still, food for the soul. Is your soul ever hungry, friend?" "I know not what you mean," answered the old man. "I have a soul, I know, for the priest tells me so; and so have my relatives who have gone before me, as I know to my cost; for they make me pay pretty roundly to get their souls out of purgatory.

The increases over suggested or mandated levels of lead in these creams and lotions ranged from 6.1 to 45.9 and from 1.2 to 9.2 mg kg-1 when compared with Cosmetic Ingredients Review Expert Panel 2007 and German safe maximum permissible limit of lead in cosmetics, respectively. Chromium And mercury were undetected in 100% of the cosmetic product. Faruruwa and Bartholomew [14] revealed that in a total of 40 samples consisting of 10 different types of facial cosmetics commonly used in Nigeria, Chromium, nickel, zinc and iron were found in varying concentrations in all the samples, 85% of the samples also contain Cd while 18 of the 40 samples have Pb above detection limit (0.20-31.70 mg kg-1). The levels of Pb and Cd in superstores and open markets were lower in comparison to other metals under considerations, while the concentration of Fe is generally high (72.90-261275.60 mg kg-1) with one of the powders having the highest value of 261275.60 mg kg-1. The lowest value 72.90 mg kg-1 was found in face cleanser. In another study published in Kano State, Nigeria, a total of 20 skin powder products were sampled from Sabon Gari (Bata) market with the aim of detecting the presence of cadmium and chromium. All the metals were detected in all the samples, even though, at different concentrations (P 0.050). The concentration of chromium was lower when compared to cadmium [15]. Due to the spuriousness of these cosmetic products in developing and under developed countries such as Nigeria, the facial cosmetics are being sold under the brand name of well reputed national and international companies in both open markets and superstores in the country. Considering the different conditions of sales, which could possibly affect the heavy metals content of these cosmetics, coupled with the lack of regulations on cosmetics in the country and also marred with counterfeiting of cosmetic products, both markets faces non- regulations and the unfounded believe that genuine and safer products are found in the bigger and more expensive market like the superstores than in the smaller and less expensive market like the open market. In addition, Kano is a well known state for its commercial activities spanning across various products including cosmetics. These cosmetics are been channeled to different parts of the country for use. However, the complete profile of heavy metals in cosmetics in the state is lacking. Similarly, there is a higher patronage of these products from people of different ages and level of literacy because of the immense quest for beauty. Therefore, the need arises to investigate the heavy metal contents of cosmetics in the state. This research was aimed at determining the concentration of some heavy metals in cosmetic products in Kano metropolis through the determination of the concentration of Copper, Manganese, Nickel, Chromium, Cadmium and Lead in skin lightening creams, face powder and lipsticks.

The most damning indictment of the prosecution's case came from none other than the ICTY's own chief investigator, Jean-Pierre Rioux, who testified that the prosecution's star witness, General Wesley Clark, had perjured himself on the stand. This bombshell revelation was promptly swept under the rug by the court, but it has left many observers wondering how much of the prosecution's evidence is similarly tainted. Meanwhile, the prosecution's attempts to link Milosevic to the atrocities committed during the Balkan wars have been woefully inadequate. The ICTY's own rules require that the prosecution prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Milosevic had "command responsibility" for the crimes committed by Serbian forces. Yet, despite months of testimony from supposed "insiders" and "experts," the prosecution has failed to produce a single shred of credible evidence linking Milosevic to the worst atrocities. In fact, many of the prosecution's key witnesses have been discredited or have recanted their testimony. The most egregious example is that of Ratomir Tanic, a former Serbian intelligence officer who initially testified that Milosevic had ordered the massacre of Bosnian Muslims at Srebrenica. However, it later emerged that Tanic had been coached by the prosecution and had fabricated his testimony in exchange for a reduced sentence. The prosecution's desperation has become increasingly apparent as the trial has dragged on. In a bizarre move, Nice QC recently attempted to introduce a "new" piece of evidence - a video allegedly showing Milosevic ordering the massacre of Albanian civilians in Kosovo. However, it was quickly revealed that the video was a crude forgery, and the prosecution was forced to withdraw it from evidence. In light of these developments, it is little wonder that the ICTY is considering a "radical review" of the proceedings. The court's credibility is at stake, and it is clear that the prosecution's case is on the verge of collapse. The question is, will the ICTY have the courage to admit defeat and acquit Milosevic, or will it continue to twist and manipulate the evidence to secure a conviction at any cost? One thing is certain: the world will be watching closely as this farcical trial continues to unfold.

On the brow of the opposite hill, arising from a grove of cypresses and pines, the airy shafts of the cloisters of San Cataldo pierced the translucent air. The uplifted cross caught the last rays of the sun, whose misty, crimson ball was slowly sinking below the world's dark rim. Slowly the horseman started on the winding descent into the valley below, thence on the steep climb of the opposite heights, passing numerous groups of peasants, in grotesque, gaily tinted garbs, who stood or knelt round the wayside shrine of a saint, their bronzed countenances aglow with fervor and religious zeal. Some pilgrims, known by bearing the rosemary branch, were visible among the trees in the background. - Francesco Villani was tall and of slender stature. His face possessed almost classic regularity of features. Hair of chestnut brown, pointing to an extraction not purely Italian, clustered round the high forehead. His eyes, gazing wistfully from the well-poised head, were the brown eyes of a dreamer. His age might have been reckoned at twenty-five. His appearance and bearing were those of one bred in the sphere of a court. His garb consisted of a russet-colored tunic, fastened with a belt of embossed leather studded with gold, particolored hose, encased in leather buskins, and a cap with a slanting plume, the ensemble denoting a page of some princely household. A shadowy wilderness encompassed the ascent to the cloisters, whose white walls were sharply outlined against the greenish-blue of the sky. The scene which on all sides met the youth's gaze seemed almost unreal. Laden with perfume was the air, of jessamine, of styrax, of roses heavy in the breathless evening glow. Here and there, under drooping branches, he passed a wooden cross, rudely carved, marking the resting-place of some unknown pilgrim, or early martyr of the faith. Wandering ivy wound its tendrils round the faded or half-effaced inscriptions, and ilex foliage drooped thickly over the Memento Mori on the roadside. The hour added to the beauty of the scene. A silver moon, hovering midway in the eastern sky, began to scintillate with trembling lustre on the dreaming world below. An intermittent breeze now and then swayed the tops of the stately holm-oaks, wafting the fragrance of almond-trees and oleander along alleys bordered by yew-trees. A nightingale poured forth its plaintive song from the shelter of branch-shadowed thickets, and from the high-domed chapel of the cloisters came the muffled chant of the monks, borne along on the wings of the evening breeze. At last the summit was reached. Francesco stopped before the massive gates of San Cataldo. With a quick tightening of the lips he dismounted. Then, without a second's pause, he seized upon the rope which sounded a gong in the porter's lodge. "Who is it that would enter?" drawled a surly voice, quaverous with age.

Once again the screenplay, by director Brian Dannelly and Michael Urban, is pointed: "Mercy House doesn't really exist for the people that go there, but for the people who send them," says Patrick, who is having his own rebellion against Pastor Skip, and casts his lot with the rebels. Lazying it up further by quoting from James Berardinelli's review to express my opinion of the movie: The film's main flaw - the kind of narrow-mindedness of which it ironically accuses its subjects (in this case, the less religious a character, the more positively they are portrayed) - might be forgivable if Saved! made an interesting or original point/.../. But /.../ the characters are developed in facile ways, and [the] message lacks subtlety. Just because I may sympathize with some of what [it] has to say doesn't mean I'm impressed by the way [it says it]. Sermonizing is sermonizing, regardless of whether the doctrine being preached is based on the Bible of the Church or the Bible of Liberal Politics. [Religion is treated] as a disease, not a life choice. It's something people need to be cured of in order to live a meaningful life. (Maybe they don't have to give it up altogether, but the fundamentalist aspect needs to go.) In order to refine this point, Mary is made increasingly sympathetic the further she drifts from her beliefs. Most of the "true believers," like Pastor Skip, Mary's mother, and Hilary Faye, are shown to be hypocrites. And the sympathetic supporters are non-believers Roland and Cassandra. It doesn't take long before it's apparent that [the] objective with this film is not just to lampoon fundamentalism, but to express contempt for it. In this world, the path to salvation comes through renouncing Jesus, not embracing him. To end on a more personal and positive note, I'd like to mention some of the actors and say that I blame the script for any faults of their characters, not their acting abilities. I've never seen a bad performance by Jena Malone in any of her many movies, and she's not bad here either. I was happy to see Marie-Louise Parker in it as I adore her Amy Gardner character on the West Wing. It's great to see Macaulay Culkin back on the screen again, especially as he's quite good in this one. Finally, the actress who is the reason I saw this movie in the first place, Mandy Moore. I've eagerly awaited every one of her movies especially since her first one A Walk To Remember turned out so good. Unfortunately none of her following movies have been as good, but her individual performance have always been good. She has consistently proven herself to be more than just a pop-princess, both in acting and singing. For example, her latest record, Coverage, contains covers of songs from the '70s and '80s and is surprisingly good.

The use of additives as a supplementary measure to reduce NOx emissions from coal combustion has gained significant attention in recent years. These additives can be categorized into two main groups: fuel additives and combustion additives. Fuel additives are typically added to the coal prior to combustion, whereas combustion additives are injected into the combustion chamber during the combustion process. Fuel additives, such as calcium magnesium acetate, have been shown to reduce NOx emissions by up to 20% [7]. These additives work by altering the combustion chemistry, reducing the formation of NOx precursors. Combustion additives, on the other hand, can be more effective, with some achieving NOx reductions of up to 40% [8]. These additives, such as ammonia or urea, react with NOx in the combustion chamber, converting it into harmless nitrogen and water. One of the main advantages of using additives is their relatively low cost compared to installing SCR or SNCR systems. Additionally, additives can be easily retrofitted to existing power plants, making them an attractive option for plants that are nearing the end of their operational life. However, the effectiveness of additives can vary greatly depending on the type of coal being used, the combustion conditions, and the specific additive employed. Furthermore, the use of additives may also have unintended consequences, such as increased particulate matter emissions or ash fouling [9]. Another potential solution is the use of advanced coal combustion technologies, such as oxyfuel combustion or chemical looping combustion. These technologies have the potential to reduce NOx emissions by up to 90% [10]. Oxyfuel combustion involves burning coal in pure oxygen instead of air, producing a flue gas that is mostly CO2 and water vapor. This flue gas can then be easily captured and stored, reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Chemical looping combustion, on the other hand, involves the use of a metal oxide to convert coal into CO2 and H2O, which can then be separated and captured. While these advanced technologies hold great promise, they are still in the early stages of development and face significant technical and economic challenges before they can be widely adopted. In the short term, the use of additives and primary NOx reduction strategies will likely remain the most cost-effective way to comply with stricter emission limits. However, as the global energy landscape continues to evolve, it is clear that a multi-faceted approach will be necessary to address the complex issue of NOx emissions from coal combustion. In conclusion, the reduction of NOx emissions from coal combustion is a critical step towards mitigating the environmental impacts of fossil fuel-based power generation. While significant progress has been made in reducing NOx emissions, much work remains to be done to achieve the stringent emission limits set by the IED. The use of additives, advanced coal combustion technologies, and primary NOx reduction strategies will all play important roles in achieving this goal. As the global energy sector continues to transition towards a more sustainable future, it is essential that we continue to develop and deploy innovative solutions to address the environmental impacts of coal combustion. References: [7] Li et al. (2019). Fuel additives for NOx reduction in coal combustion. Energy & Fuels, 33(2), 1231-1240. [8] Wang et al. (2020). Combustion additives for NOx reduction in coal-fired power plants. Journal of Cleaner Production, 286, 120934. [9] Chen et al. (2018). Effects of additives on particulate matter emissions from coal combustion. Fuel, 211, 831-839. [10] Kuivalainen et al. (2019). Advanced coal combustion technologies for NOx reduction.

OFF DUTY CLOTHING: Within the confines of Tent City, personal attire must still reflect the professionalism expected of USAF personnel. Clothing must not display offensive language or graphics, promoting a respectful environment for all residents. Shorts and T-shirts are acceptable when on personal time but must be neat and not excessively revealing. Ensure that footwear is worn at all times outside of sleeping quarters, as protection against sharp objects or other potential hazards. Safety remains a priority, even in leisure activities. QUIET HOURS: To maintain the morale and well-being of everyone residing in Tent City, quiet hours are strictly observed between 2200 and 0600 hours. During this time, any activity that could disturb others, such as loud conversations or the playing of musical instruments, is prohibited. This rule is in place to ensure that all members, who may be on different duty cycles, have the opportunity to rest adequately. SANITATION AND HYGIENE: Cleanliness is paramount to prevent illness and maintain a healthy living environment. Personal hygiene is expected to be upheld through regular use of shower and laundry facilities. The maintenance of tents and shared spaces is a collective responsibility. After utilizing common areas like bathrooms or picnics spots, ensure they are left in a clean state for the next user. SMOKING: Smoking is only permitted in designated areas clearly marked within the compound. This regulation is in place to manage fire hazards and promote the health of all personnel. The smoking areas are equipped with containers for disposal of butts, and these should be used to avoid littering. COMMUNICATIONS: To maintain operational security, be mindful of discussions held within Tent City that pertain to missions or sensitive information. It is advised to minimize the use of personal electronic devices when discussing operational activities. Information dissemination should follow the chain of command, and discretion must be used in all communications, both verbal and written. INTEGRITY AND RESPECT: The key values of integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do are cornerstones of life in Tent City. Residents are expected to treat each other with respect and courtesy, irrespective of rank or nationality. Any form of harassment or discrimination will not be tolerated and should be reported immediately through the appropriate channels. AUTHORIZED ELECTRONICS: Laptops and personal entertainment devices such as music players are allowed but should be used considerately to avoid disruptions. Unauthorized electronic equipment that could interfere with operations is prohibited. Always secure valuables, and report any lost or stolen items promptly to security forces. CAMP CARE: Participate in the Camp Pride Program by setting aside time each week to help maintain and improve Tent City. Whether it's by picking up litter, organizing storage areas, or assisting in facility maintenance, each contribution enhances the quality of life for everyone. WEATHER AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS: Stay informed about weather conditions and be prepared for rapid changes such as sandstorms or heatwaves. Adequate hydration and protection against the sun are essential. Follow directives during any environmental alerts issued by security forces or the command group. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES: Familiarize yourself with emergency procedures displayed throughout Tent City. Fire drills and other emergency scenario training will occur regularly. Your prompt and orderly participation in these exercises is crucial to ensuring readiness and safety for all residents.

As my mind attempted to juggle the absurdity of my nocturnal commitments, my consciousness drifted deeper into a serene landscape that defied the chronology and logic of the waking world. The scene unfolded seamlessly, as if some benevolent dream-master were guiding me through an intricate tapestry of bygone eras. I found myself walking along a sun-dappled path, the gravel crunching softly beneath my feet, leading to a stately manor nestled at the edge of a whispering wood. It was undoubtedly English, with a pleasing symmetry and gentle grandeur, its honey-coloured stone glowing warmly in the dreamlight. Turrets reached skyward, ornamented with ivy that clung lovingly to the walls, weaving a story of resilience and time. I could discern every mullion, every rogation of leaded glass. As the windows welcomed the breeze, I caught the faintest hint of music-the playful sound of a lute-drifting from within, like a sweet invitation to enter. The path veered gently, guiding me toward an arched door that creaked open as I approached, welcoming me to cross its threshold. With a curious mix of anticipation and tranquility, I stepped inside. In the hook task, children appeared to understand that a hook would be the most functional tool; in a tool selection version of the task, children as young as 4 years chose the hooked tool over the straight tool first when their task was to retrieve a bucket from a vertical tube using pre-made tools (Beck et al., 2011, Experiment 1). Furthermore, children could also recognize a functional tool when shown how to make one: After initial failure on the hook innovation task, children readily manufactured a hook tool and used it correctly when shown a hook-making demonstration (Beck et al., 2011; Cutting et al., 2011). Note that children were only shown how to make the required tool; they were not given a demonstration as to how to use it. Taken together, this evidence suggests that it is not a simple lack of knowledge that limits children's performance. Children understand the properties of the materials they are given and are aware that they are allowed to manipulate them. Children understand the physics of the task and can recognize a hook as the most functional tool. So, if children possess all of this knowledge, why do they find tool innovation so difficult? One possibility is that children's difficulty with tool innovation could be due to its ill-structured nature. Although there is no single agreed-on definition of what constitutes an ill-structured problem, a generally agreed-on framework is that an ill-structured problem is one that is missing information from its start state, goal state, or information regarding the transformation required to go between the two (Goel & Grafman, 2000; Wood, 1983). Following this definition, tool innovation is an ill-structured problem; children are given the start state (the apparatus and the materials) and told that the goal is to retrieve the sticker, yet they are given no information regarding how they should go about this task. Compare this with Beck and colleagues' (2011, Experiment 1) well-structured tool selection task in which young children readily succeed. In this task, children are given the start state (the apparatus and materials) and the goal state (retrieve the sticker) and are given the choice between two possible means for effecting a transformation (use the straight pipecleaner or use the hooked pipecleaner). When information about the start state, goal, and means were provided, children found it trivially easy to retrieve the bucket. Current findings suggest that just having all of the individual items of domain knowledge is not sufficient to be successful in solving ill-structured problems (Chen & Bradshaw, 2007). Domain knowledge must be well integrated into what is termed structural knowledge to enable people to use it effectively (Jonassen, Beissner, & Yacci, 1993). Structural knowledge is knowledge that is well integrated and developed and, as such, allows the person to use this knowledge in a flexible manner.

And the party's presidential nominee, unlike Al Gore four years ago, is not running away from the president who preceded him. So what? It's pretty clear that the Democrats are united because they hate Bush. But this doesn't tell us anything about whether or not the country is becoming more polarized. Indeed, if anything, it suggests that the opposite may be true. If the Democrats are so divided, how could they unite behind someone like John Kerry? They couldn't. A third sign of partisanship is the ability to motivate voters to go to the polls, and here too both parties seem to have found ways to mobilize their bases. Turnout was up substantially in the primaries, and the number of new registrants continues to grow. Again, this tells us nothing about whether the country is more polarized. It only tells us that the parties are doing a good job of getting out the vote. Voter registration does not equal polarization. Finally, there is the way the parties are presenting themselves to the public. In the past, each side tried to appeal to the other. This time, neither wants anything to do with the other. No one seems interested in reaching across the aisle, no one talks about bipartisanship, no one speaks of compromise. To paraphrase the old saying, "Politics ain't beanbag." Political campaigns are about winning votes. Parties will try to win votes any way they can. Sometimes this means appealing to your opponent's base. Other times, it means trying to get your own base fired up. These are tactical decisions, not evidence of some deep divide in America. The fact that the two sides are fighting hard doesn't mean they're not close together ideologically. Both sides are fighting hard because the electorate is split almost down the middle. There aren't many swing voters out there, which means that the parties need to squeeze every possible vote out of their respective bases. If the country were truly divided into two camps, we wouldn't expect such fierce competition. We would instead see the parties resting comfortably on their natural constituencies. As it happens, there is an alternative explanation for all this activity. Americans are more partisan than ever because they are increasingly divided along ideological lines. For most of our history, political parties existed to distribute patronage jobs, not to fight ideological battles. Now, however, they have become vehicles for the expression of ideas. The Republican Party is dominated by conservatives, while liberals hold sway among the Democrats. Ideological division isn't the same thing as partisanship. And ideology itself is often just a cover for special interests. The GOP is certainly more conservative than it used to be, but the Democrats are still a hodgepodge of interest groups. Neither party is particularly coherent ideologically. Moreover, the fact that the parties have become more ideological doesn't prove that the country is more polarized. Most Americans remain moderate on the issues. If anything, the country has become more liberal over the last couple of decades. The GOP has moved to the right, but the Dems haven't really moved to the left. If anything, they've moved slightly to the right. The result is a larger gap between the parties, but not necessarily between the people. This situation leaves little room for moderates, and indeed, there are fewer of them than ever. Most Americans, according to recent surveys, identify either with the right or the left. Fewer describe themselves as centrists. Centrism is no longer a virtue; it is a vice. Well, first off, I'm not sure this is true. Certainly, most Americans identify with a particular party, but that doesn't mean they're necessarily extreme.

In a jiffy the boys scattered in all directions in search of firewood; up the side of the hill and along the near bank of a noisy mountain stream, and soon were returning with armfuls of dead wood. Most of them were experienced in building camp fires in true frontier style, and the work progressed rapidly. Two of the boys, Hal Kenyon and Byron Bowler, were delegated to the work of starting the fire. This was not done by striking a match and touching it to some dry leaves. The method employed was one more suited to the romantic scene. First, Hal and Byron searched until they found two serviceable pieces of dry cottonwood root. Having good, strong, sharp pocketknives, they proceeded to whittle and shave the roots. One was made flat and about three-fourths of an inch thick; the other was cut slim and round and sharpened at both ends. In one edge of the flat piece was cut a notch, and close to the notch was sunk a hole to fit one end of the slim piece. Then a small hand-piece with a socket for the other end of the drill was prepared by Byron, while Hal cut a section of a small green limb, two feet long, which with a thong made a bow. All the material needed for starting a fire was now ready save a supply of tinder. This was obtained by rubbing a piece of dry cedar on a rough boulder, producing a handful of easily lighted shreds. The notched piece of wood was now placed on a flat rock, the drill was inserted in place and the string of the bow looped tightly over it. Then the top-socket-piece was set on the other end for a handle, and the bow was drawn back and forth, the notched piece being held in place under the foot of the operator. Hal Kenyon operated the device. The drill revolved rapidly in the socket, and presently a fine brown powder was flowing into the notch. In a few seconds this powder was smoking densely and slight fanning with a hat brought a flame. Some of the tinder was now applied and after a little blowing, a tiny flame leaped up. The rest of the tinder was then applied, followed by some cedar bark and small wood. Pretty soon the fire was roaring and crackling, while the boys piled on more fuel. "Now for our camp-fire yell," cried Hal when the last armful of fuel had been deposited on the burning heap. Immediately the canyon rang and echoed with thirty young voices chanting the following: "Camp-fire, rah! Smoke-punk, ha! Tinder, Lakefarm! Rah - rah - rah!"

The indirect effects, on the other hand, are the subsequent consequences of the initial shock, which can manifest in various forms, such as changes in consumption patterns, altered investment decisions, and shifts in labor market dynamics (Cavallo & Noy, 2010). These indirect effects can have far-reaching implications, perpetuating the impact of the disaster beyond the immediate aftermath. For instance, a natural disaster can lead to a decline in agricultural production, resulting in reduced food availability and increased prices, which can, in turn, exacerbate food insecurity and malnutrition among vulnerable populations (FAO, 2013). Moreover, the destruction of infrastructure, such as roads and bridges, can disrupt supply chains, leading to shortages of essential goods and services, further exacerbating the humanitarian crisis (UNISDR, 2015). The modeling framework must also account for the role of feedback loops, which can either mitigate or amplify the impact of the disaster. For example, a well-functioning early warning system can enable timely evacuations, reducing the loss of life and property, whereas inadequate preparedness can lead to a higher toll (Okuyama, 2007). Similarly, the presence of effective social safety nets can help cushion the impact of the disaster, while their absence can exacerbate the vulnerability of affected populations (Kahn, 2005). Furthermore, the framework must consider the geographical dimension of the disaster, recognizing that the impact of the shock can vary significantly across different regions, with areas closer to the epicenter typically experiencing more severe damage (Skoufias, 2003). In order to develop a comprehensive understanding of the post-disaster dynamics, it is essential to integrate these various components into a cohesive modeling framework. This framework should be capable of capturing the complex interactions between the physical environment, the economy, and the social systems, as well as the feedback loops that shape the disaster response and recovery process. By doing so, policymakers and disaster risk reduction practitioners can better anticipate the potential consequences of natural disasters, identify vulnerable populations, and design targeted interventions to mitigate the impact of these events. Ultimately, the development of such a framework can contribute to the reduction of disaster risk and the promotion of sustainable development in low-income regions. One potential approach to developing this framework is to employ a spatially explicit, agent-based modeling approach, which can simulate the behavior of individual households, firms, and institutions in response to the disaster (Duckers, Frerks, & Birkmann, 2015). This approach can capture the spatial heterogeneity of the disaster impact, as well as the complex interactions between different agents and the environment. Additionally, the model can be parameterized using empirical data on disaster-related indicators, such as damage estimates, mortality rates, and displacement figures, to ensure that the simulations are grounded in reality. By integrating the insights from the literature on disaster risk reduction, economics, and geography, a comprehensive modeling framework can be developed to analyze the complex dynamics of natural disasters in low-income regions. This framework can provide policymakers with a valuable tool for predicting the potential consequences of natural disasters, identifying vulnerable populations, and designing targeted interventions to mitigate the impact of these events. Ultimately, the development of such a framework can contribute to the reduction of disaster risk and the promotion of sustainable development in low-income regions.

The family had been known as "the reckless Burnets" ever since the Georgian days, when the sixth Viscount had, in one night at Crockford's, gambled away the whole of his vast Yorkshire estate, and his son on the following night lost forty-five thousand guineas at the same table. Dare-devilry ran in the Scarcliff blood. From the Wars of the Roses down to the present day the men had always been fearless soldiers - for some of their armour, and that of their retainers, still stood in long, grim rows in the dark-panelled gallery where we were - and the women had always been notable for their beauty, as proved by the famous portraits by Gainsborough, Lawrence, Lely, Reynolds, Hoppner, and others, that hung in the splendid gallery beyond. But surely none of those time-mellowed portraits that I could see from where I stood was half so beautiful as the little friend of my youth beside me. In those long-past days of our boy-and-girl affection she had been very fragile and very beautiful, with wondrous hair of that unusual gold-brown tint, and eyes of clear bright blue. But even now, at twenty-three, she had in no way lost her almost child-like grace and charm. Those deep blue eyes, turned upon me in mock reproach, were still fathomless, her cheeks were perfect in their symmetry, her mouth smiling and sweet, and her brows well arched and well defined, while her chin, slightly protruding, gave her that piquant air that was so delightful. Though unmarried, she was entirely unconventional, just as the Scarcliffs had ever been. Smart London knew Tibbie well. Some day she would many, people said, but the wiseacres shook their heads and secretly pitied the man who became her husband. As a friend Tibbie was perfect. She was a man's woman. She could shoot or fish, she would play bridge and pay up honourably, she rode well, and she drove her 60 h.p. "Mercedes" better even than her own chauffeur. Old Lady Scarcliff - a delightful old person - had long ago given her up as hopeless. It was all Cynthia's doing, for, truth to tell, her extravagances and her utter disregard for the convenances were the outcome of her residence with the Wydcombes. I own frankly that I was sorry to see this change in her. The slim, rather prudish little love of my youth had now developed into that loud-speaking, reckless type of smart woman who nowadays is so much in evidence in Society. I much preferred her as I had known her years ago when my father and hers were intimate friends, and when I came so often to stay at Ryhall. True, our friendship had been a firm one always, but alas! I now detected a great change in her. Though so handsome, she was, as I had so very frankly told her, not exactly the kind of woman I should choose as a wife.

Such research projects are still ongoing paving the way toward optimization of the full life cycle of lithium-ion batteries utilized in the automotive sector, from material management issues, through use phase, to their reuse/recycling stage [21]. Biodiesel is the most promising alternative fuel for diesel engines [22,23] and can be produced from a variety of vegetable oils and animal fats [24-26]. Among the different methods for biodiesel production, transesterification is regarded as the most popular process in the industry since it provides the highest conversion efficiency and at the lowest cost [27,28]. Transesterification is a reaction in which triglycerides reacts with an alcohol in the presence of a catalyst (to improve the reaction rate and yield) to produce esters and glycerol [29-32]. Different types of enzymes as well as homogeneous/heterogeneous acids or base catalysts are conventionally used for transesterification reaction. Nevertheless, some advanced methods for biodiesel production has been proposed in order to improve the efficiency, simplicity or cost of the process, such as nanocatalytic [33], ultrasound-assisted [34,35], microwave-assisted [36], in-situ transesterification [37], supercritical fluid (SCF) [38], superheated vapor (SHV) [39], subcritical [40], and membrane-assisted technologies [41]. Since catalytic reactions come with a lot of disadvantages [42], researchers developed some non-catalytic alternative methods such as SCF and SHV. These processes could facilitate the easy separation of products [42], increasing the rate of reaction (and thus efficiency) [42], and eliminating the necessity of pre-treatment steps for various feedstock (and thus reducing costs) [43-45]. Further explanation of SCF and SHV technologies could be found in Karmakar and Halder [42]. Beside the mentioned development in biodiesel production processes, there is also a great focus on plant genetic engineering for sustainable biodiesel production. In such context, production of high performance-oil plants varieties for commercial biodiesel production could be achieved through next generation sequencing (NGS), omics technologies, and genetic engineering pathways [46]. Biodiesel combustion results in less air pollution compared to petroleum diesel due to its higher oxygen content and lacking of sulfur and aromatic compounds [47,48]. More specifically, biodiesel combustion results in less PM, CO, and unburned hydrocarbons (UHC) emissions [49-51]. In this regard, biodiesel could also be a promising alternative for urban buses that are the primary source for high levels of PM and CO emissions in urban areas. Apart from the mentioned advantages of biodiesel, a number of studies have also reported increases in NOx emissions in response to biodiesel inclusion in fossil diesel [52-54]. However, there is no general agreement in this regard in the published literature [55-58], and the results differ with fuel properties, engine characteristics, as well as the operating conditions. For example, a comprehensive review on NOx formation mechanism showed that several factors could contribute to an increase in NOx emissions from biodiesel combustion [59].

Two younger girls, with arms linked and heads close together, had come into view in a distant corner of the garden, walking decorously, as befitted their white dresses. It was the taller of the two, a brown-faced girl of fifteen, with dark curls and extremely long slim legs, who had caught sight of the boy walking towards the house, and had promptly acted as though electrified. She relinquished her companion's arms, uttered an incoherent exclamation, and dashed wildly across the lawn, taking the flower bed that bordered it with a flying leap. The sound of the racing feet made the boy swing round quickly. Then a smile broadened on his face, and his eyes twinkled. They pumped each other's hands enthusiastically. "Oh, Wally!" said Norah, breathlessly. "Oh, you old brick!" Wally Meadows laughed outright. "You don't know what a blue funk I've been in," he said. "This is a horribly scary place to come to alone-and I've been picturing you made as prim and proper as all these girls seem to be. But you're not!" "Indeed, I'm not," Norah answered. "And no more are they!" "Aren't they, really?" asked Wally, much interested. "Well, they look it; there's a girl over there with red hair who looks nearly too good to be true"-wherein Mr. Meadows showed as much penetration as is usually given to man. "You don't mean to say that they're all accustomed to getting across a flower bed in your fashion, Norah?" "Oh, I'll get into a dreadful row if Miss Winter happened to see me, I expect!" Norah said. "It's against the rules, of course-but I had to run or to yell, or I'd have missed you-and it's riskier to yell. Oh, Wally, I am glad to see you!" "So am I," said Wally, heartily-"to see you, I mean. You've grown immense, too, Norah." "Yes, haven't I? All my frocks are too short, and I know Dad will say I've put my feet too far through them. Oh, Wally, have you seen Dad-and Jim?" "Saw them yesterday. They ought to be here pretty soon-but my brother motored me down, so I didn't come with them. Norah-there's a girl looking at me, and if you don't take her away I shall scream!" "Why, that's Jean Yorke," said Norah, wheeling. "She's my chum, and you've got to be extra nice to her, 'cause she is coming home with me for the holidays." "Then she deserves any one's kind sympathy," said Wally, solemnly. He advanced upon Jean with outstretched hand and a smile that went far to put that somewhat shy individual at her ease, while Norah murmured a haphazard introduction. Jean was a short and rather thickset person, with blue eyes and a freckled nose, and a square, honest face.

The consequence was, that the illustrious house of Lavender was ready to do anything in the world for that excellent Mr Beaufort, who had fished their heir out of troubles unknown; and, in respect to that heir himself, were bending all their faculties to the task of getting him married, and so put out of harm's way. It was a new sphere for the mental vivacity and curiosity of Millefleurs. He devoted himself to a study of the young ladies of the highest civilisation, just as he had devoted himself to the life of the dockyards and the backwoods. (Probably I should say to the mines and the cattle-ranches; but the reader who knows the fashion will here supply the appropriate phrase.) He found the study curious, and not at all unpleasant, and so went about scattering wild hopes about him wherever he moved. Was anything else possible? If the young ladies in our northern county had been (inevitably) fluttered and excited when Pat Torrance fixed his big light eyes upon them, knowing the value of him as, so to speak, an appointment, a post for life which would remove all anxiety about their future comfort from their own minds and those of their parents, how much more when the Marquis of Millefleurs went hopping about the drawing-rooms, carrying on his researches in a far more genial and agreeable manner than Pat Torrance was capable of doing? And it was quite certain that nobody would ever be unhappy with Millefleurs. He was always cheerful, always considerate, ready to do anything for anybody. He was more like a daughter than a son, the Duchess declared, with tears in her eyes - foreseeing what she wanted, watching over her as nobody had ever done before: although it was no doubt very wrong - oh, very wrong! - to almost break her heart, leaving her two years without a letter; but he would not do so to his wife. Thus the - we will not say candidates, rather nominees - possible occupants of the delightful and every way desirable post of Marchioness of Millefleurs had every sort of inducement to "go in" for it, and scarcely any drawback at all. The drawback was not worth speaking of - it was the most superficial of objections. This enterprising, amusing, good-tempered, quick-witted, accomplished, and lovable hero, was, as the girls said, the funniest little man that had ever been seen. He was shorter than most of the young ladies to whom he made himself so agreeable. He was plump and round, a succession of curves and gently billowing outlines; his eyes were like little black beads, though they were sparkling with life and animation; he had a round face like a boy of ten, with nice little puffy rosy cheeks, and a lisp which completed the infantile effect of his appearance generally.

So there we were, Steve and I, just trying to figure out what on earth we were going to do. We called everyone we knew and then some, trying to find someone who might be in the area, or at least had a reliable mechanic nearby. Hours went by, and just as we were about to give up and start preparing for a night under the stars, I got a direct message on Instagram. This message was from Claudia, offering help. She told me she was nearby, and insisted that she come out to where we were with some cold drinks and snacks while we sorted out our plan. And let me tell you, that was the turning point of our entire day. It was such a relief to meet a friendly face who understood what it meant to be stuck in the middle of nowhere with horses. Claudia showed up with a huge smile, and even though we hadn't met before, it felt like meeting an old friend. She managed to get in touch with a local mechanic she trusted, and thanks to her, we had the truck back on the road by Tuesday afternoon. But even more important than the mechanical assistance was the camaraderie she brought. We spent hours just chatting, learning about each other's journeys and aspirations. And that's how I learned about her amazing ski-touring adventures. Steve: That sounds incredible. Claudia, you're like the hero of this story. Claudia: Well, it's what you do in the community, right? You help each other out. I'm just glad I could be there at the right time. And, it was a pleasant surprise to find out that I was helping out someone with such a prominent place in our shared world. Janice: It definitely was a memorable experience! So, Claudia, as we dive into the ski touring sport, tell us, what drew you to it, especially coming from such a strong background in equine sports? Claudia: You know, it's funny because the skills you develop in horseback riding - balance, rhythm, understanding movement - they all translate surprisingly well to ski touring. A couple of friends out here in Montana were absolutely obsessed with it, and they invited me along on one of their tours. I fell in love instantly. There's an incredible sense of freedom and exploration you get out there on the trails. It's a blend of adventure and serenity that I hadn't quite found anywhere else. Steve: That sounds absolutely exhilarating. What's a typical day out on the slopes for you? Claudia: We usually start super early, just after dawn, when the snow is pristine and the world is quiet and still. It's a lot about preparation - making sure you have all the right gear and that your route is planned. Then, there's the trek uphill, which is actually one of the most rewarding parts. The payoff, of course, is reaching a summit with stunning views and then skiing down. It's this mix of physical endurance, breathtaking beauty, and thrilling descents that keeps me coming back for more. Janice: It sounds like you found another passion that enhances your life just as much as the horses do. We might just have to try ski touring ourselves after this chat!

The Ishikawa cell-based assay has been designed to mimic the human uterine response to estrogenic compounds, using a cell line that is known to express estrogen receptors and exhibit estrogen-dependent gene expression (Kanda et al., 2001). The assay measures the induction of estrogen-responsive genes, such as progesterone receptor (PGR) and cyclin D1 (CCND1), as well as the inhibition of estrogen-dependent cell proliferation. In preliminary studies, the assay has been shown to be sensitive and specific for detecting estrogenic compounds, including those with known uterotropic activity (Miller et al., 2017). To further validate the utility of the Ishikawa cell-based assay, we have compared its performance to the traditional uterotrophic assay in a series of experiments. In these studies, we have exposed cells to a range of estrogenic compounds, including estradiol, bisphenol A, and genistein, and measured the induction of estrogen-responsive genes and inhibition of cell proliferation. Our results show that the Ishikawa cell-based assay is able to detect estrogenic activity with high sensitivity and specificity, and that the results are comparable to those obtained with the uterotrophic assay (Miller et al., 2018). In addition to its potential use as a replacement for the uterotrophic assay, the Ishikawa cell-based assay may also be useful for identifying estrogenic compounds that have been missed by traditional in vitro assays. For example, some estrogenic compounds may not exhibit estrogenic activity in traditional cell-based assays, but may still induce uterotropic effects in vivo. The Ishikawa cell-based assay may be able to detect these compounds by measuring the induction of estrogen-responsive genes and inhibition of cell proliferation. The development of the Ishikawa cell-based assay is an important step towards the development of a more comprehensive and human-relevant approach to assessing the estrogenic potential of chemicals. By using a cell line that is known to express estrogen receptors and exhibit estrogen-dependent gene expression, we can better mimic the human uterine response to estrogenic compounds and gain a better understanding of the potential risks associated with exposure to these compounds. In the future, we plan to continue to validate the performance of the Ishikawa cell-based assay and to explore its potential use in a variety of applications, including risk assessment and regulatory decision-making.

The Dutch, who had settled themselves in this island, protected the new government, and it continued till the death of the husband, when it devolved to his widow, who succeeded admirably well, and died rich, having amassed considerable wealth in her time, which she distributed among the natives. She married one of her subjects, a young man of a very good understanding and excellent character. Her daughter, who was married to the son of the former governor, lived long after her parents, and is still alive, though advanced in years, and has preserved the same benevolence which distinguished her ancestors. My father, having taken in what he wanted, proceeded on his voyage without any farther adventure, and arrived safe at Ceylon. Here he found his uncle dead, and his nephew, the son of his sister, in possession of the government. He was a young man about three-and-twenty years of age, of a noble and generous mind, and most remarkably handsome. He received us kindly, gave my father a house in town, and another in the country, presented him with a horse, and every thing else necessary to make us comfortable, and was particularly kind to me, who he called his little brother. In a few days we went together to see the governor's country-seat, situated near a river, whose banks are lined with the most beautiful trees. We walked along the bank till we came to a place where there was a hollow, as if made by nature, and filled with a sweet-smelling liquid. It was surrounded by several large trees, which bore fruit not unlike apricots, but much larger, and of an agreeable taste. There was also a very pretty fountain, adorned with flowers, which played in a basin of green marble, and the whole was shaded by a grove of orange-trees. At the foot of the hill, close to the river, was a building of a circular form, which served as a summer-house. It was covered with a dome supported by pillars, and ornamented with paintings and statues of figures in bronze. This building was filled with curious and valuable pieces of china-ware. In short, it was a most delightful retreat, and my friend the governor told me, that it was consecrated to Venus. I asked him why he did not build a temple to Bacchus? "Because," answered he, "I have no wine-cellar." I then begged leave to look into the cellar; he readily granted my request, and conducted me thither. It was a spacious apartment built in the rock, and fitted up with shelves, on which stood bottles of various shapes, sizes, and colours. They were ranged in rows according to the quality and price of the liquor contained in each bottle. These liquors were collected from all parts of the world, and the most exquisite flavour and aroma imaginable. There were some very ancient ones, which my friend told me had been in his family for many generations, and which, from the time of their being put into the bottles, had never seen light, nor lost a drop of their contents. He offered me a glass of a particular species of wine, which he assured me was deliciously mild and fragrant, but I declined accepting it, saying I would rather choose for myself. I was just going to open a bottle, when he observed that there was a peculiar art in opening them, which was done by a key attached to a string, and passing round the neck of the bottle, which was then loosened by pulling the string gently, and by turning it at the same time. I attempted to do this, but unfortunately broke the bottle in my hand.

If England are to stand a chance of winning the World Cup they have to treat these games as knockout games and go to places like Cardiff and Dublin and win with confidence. England have lacked a fluid, attacking game plan since the three-Test summer tour of New Zealand in 2014. In 2003 we won the Grand Slam and we actively sought to ratchet up the pressure on the players because they needed to learn how to operate under that pressure. The result was a battle-hardended group who knew how to win away from home. There was no talk of next week or the next tournament. It was about the now. One shot, no excuses. We should not forget that England will face Wales at the World Cup in a crucial group game. There's no doubt that you want to go into that match knowing you have the beating of your opposition. But, equally, no England player should be looking beyond the game tonight. Heading into the Six Nations in 2003 we didn't talk about the World Cup. As a team we told ourselves that the Six Nations was everything and, after near-misses, we desperately wanted that Grand Slam. But even within this we remained focused that winning the next game was all that mattered. It sounds simplistic, but I just kept thinking 'if we keep winning the next game, one day we'll end up in the World Cup final.' (From left to right) England's coaching team of Mike Catt, Graham Rowntree, Stuart Lancaster and Andy Farrell were all handed six-year contract extensions by the RFU last October. As a coaching team you need to consider the future and direction of the team, and to that point we began implementing a more controlling gameplan geared towards knockout rugby. In truth, with the exception of the final game against Ireland, we didn't play spectacularly well in that tournament. But we left the Six Nations knowing we had control of our game. We beat Scotland 40-9 in our fourth match on a beautiful day at Twickenham - it was the first time Jason Robinson, Josh Lewsey and Ben Cohen played together in the back three. We played OK but not as well as the scoreline might suggest and the players' response afterwards was understated. They were obviously delighted and the atmosphere in the room was great but it was treated just like a job well done, which it was. I remember the feeling of standing in the dressing room after the game with Phil Larder and Andy Robinson before the players came back in, almost chuckling. It is an amazing thing when you can feel things going right, the energy and momentum it gives you is priceless. The same can happen to this England side: by the end of the tournament they will either look like a team capable of winning a World Cup or a team with so many questions unanswered.

It considers both resource availability and task requirements [8]. In this study, we investigate the scheduling process of a DfMA proposal, particularly in the manufacturing phase. We explore a novel method that optimises the production schedule by considering several parameters, e.g., the number of workers assigned to each task, the sequence of operations, the duration of each operation, and the capacity of the workshop. The proposed methodology can support decision-making during the design process and improve the overall performance of the project. ## Methodology The methodology presented here consists of three phases: (i) modelling, (ii) simulation, and (iii) optimisation (see Fig. 2). The first phase deals with the creation of a model of the prefabrication processes. This model is created using a Discrete Event Simulation (DES) technique, where events represent changes in states of the system. DES models are commonly used to simulate complex systems and generate data regarding the behaviour of the system under different scenarios [9]. DES is widely adopted in manufacturing industries to predict the effect of design changes in the system, to assess the performance of existing facilities, to estimate the level of resources needed, and to develop efficient schedules [10]. In the second phase, the DES model is run multiple times, simulating different scenarios. The scenarios are obtained by varying some key parameters of the model, such as the number of operators assigned to each task, the sequence of operations, etc. Each scenario represents a possible configuration of the system. During the simulations, the DES model generates data regarding the performance of the system under each scenario. These data include, for example, the total cycle time, the utilisation rate of each operator, and the average queue length for each operation. These data are collected and stored in a database. In the third phase, the data generated by the DES model are analysed to identify the best-performing scenario. This is done through the use of multi-objective optimisation algorithms. Multi-objective optimisation aims at finding solutions that minimise or maximise multiple conflicting objectives simultaneously. In our case, the objectives are related to the performance of the system, such as minimising the cycle time and maximising the utilisation rate of the operators. The optimisation algorithm searches for solutions that balance these conflicting objectives, finding a compromise between them. The result of the optimisation process is a set of non-dominated solutions, called Pareto front, representing the best trade-offs among the considered objectives. Each solution in the Pareto front corresponds to a specific configuration of the system, represented by a combination of values for the key parameters of the model. The decision-maker can then choose one of these solutions according to his/her preferences and priorities. Figure 2: Proposed methodology for the optimisation of the production schedule in a prefabrication facility. ### Modelling The DES model is created using AnyLogic software. AnyLogic is a simulation tool that allows the user to create models of complex systems using a graphical interface. It supports various types of simulations, including DES, Agent-Based Simulation (ABS), System Dynamics (SD), and Hybrid Simulation (HS). In this study, we focus on DES, which is suitable for modelling discrete processes, such as manufacturing operations. The DES model consists of entities, resources, and events. Entities represent the objects that flow through the system, such as products or orders.

I was looking for some sweetbreads. Have you any?" "Sweet bread?" echoed the ancient, grumpily. "Well, why you don' look on de store, hein? W'at you t'ink I am-de baker's cart?" Although unaware of the complexities of the French tongue and the French character, Marjorie perceived a rebuff in the old woman's words. She apologised hastily and moved away. What, she kept asking herself, could she substitute for sweetbreads? Chickens were expensive and eggs, a fabulous price. Nobody in Ottawa seemed to keep hens... "Have you any sweetbreads?" She began to feel a little hysterical. It was a funny question! No wonder the old woman answered her crossly. Have you any sweetbreads? How many times had she asked it? She thought of the game the children played-Black sheep, black sheep, have you any wool? And what on earth should she get in place of sweetbreads? Raymond was so difficult about his food. He had such a tiny and pernickety appetite... By wriggling, she gained the curb before another cart. "Have you any sweetbreads?" No one paid her the slightest heed. The centre of the stage was held by a tall, spare woman with a stridulous voice. Marjorie knew her slightly. Two weeks ago she had called-not as people called at home, in Pinto Plains-but sternly and coldly, neither giving nor receiving pleasure by the visit, save when she had laid three bits of pasteboard on the corner of the table and left the house. Mrs. Pratt was the wife of a cheerfully ineffectual professional man with political aspirations, and she felt her position keenly. So did Marjorie; and she backed away while summoning her courage to speak. "A dollar and a half?" Mrs. Pratt was saying. "Outrageous! I can't think what you people are coming to! I'll give you a dollar and a quarter, and not one penny more." She indicated a pair of frozen chickens, each with a large mauve face, that lay exposed on an old red blanket. "Can't do it, lady," said the farmer, with chattering teeth, "it cost me mor'n that to feed them this three year," and he winked heavily at the surrounding circle. "Oh, they're fowl! Well then, of course, they're not worth that much! There's a woman across the road,"-Mrs. Pratt swept her muff vaguely towards the horizon and unconsciously disarranged Marjorie's hat,-"who is selling her fowl for eighty cents!" "I'll take them," cried a woman at this juncture. "It's too cold to haggle over a few cents. Giv'um to me!" She thrust a dollar and a half into the man's hand, seized the chickens and started off. "Impertinence!" snapped Mrs. Pratt, as she turned away. Marjorie drifted on, her basket still empty.
